title: Add or change an API route
description: Keep Fastify behavior, domain and repository contracts, OpenAPI, SDKs, dashboard types, docs, and tests synchronized.
body: Start with the owning route module under packages/api/src/routes/modules . Identify the domain types, repository operations, permissions, tenant/organization/brand/event scope, runtime strings, and integration tests before editing. Change the complete slice 1. Update pure domain validation/types when business rules change. 2. Add a migration and repository method when persistence changes. 3. Implement authentication, authorization, schema, serialization, and safe errors in the route. 4. Update packages/openapi with stable operation ID, tags, security/scopes, schemas, and sanitized examples. 5. Update SDK methods/types, dashboard client types, fixtures, examples, and canonical docs. 6. Add unit, integration, tenant isolation, permission, generated client, and browser coverage as applicable. Do not reveal resource existence across scope boundaries. Do not return raw provider/database errors or secret material.

title: Add an SDK operation
description: Extend the core client and supported framework or native packages without drifting from OpenAPI or API-version support.
body: Add the operation to the canonical SDK package for its runtime, using generated/contract types where available. Preserve server/browser secret boundaries, pagination, idempotency, cancellation/timeouts, and typed error behavior. Update every supported wrapper that exposes the affected resource, then update package READMEs, the SDK guide, runnable example, snippet registry, API version statement, and parity matrix. Run the package unit tests, generated client test, demo typecheck/build, and node scripts/sdk parity matrix.mjs . A guide that compiles while its demo or export path is missing is incomplete.

title: Add documentation
description: Author validated public content, preserve canonical routes, and keep dashboard, search, redirects, and OSS export synchronized.
body: Place public long form content under docs/public . Keep plans, audits, execution evidence, and private operational detail in the repository's excluded internal documentation tree; internal content is never hidden inside a public page. Author a page Declare title, description, audience, product area, content type, stability, owner, last verified date, prerequisites, and related canonical routes. Use task outcomes, exact verification, safe failure recovery, and a next action. Do not duplicate endpoint inventories or package local installation detail. Update dependent surfaces Add or reuse a DocRouteId , update navigation, redirects, dashboard Help metadata, package links, and source inbound links. Code fences require a language and must contain no secrets, destructive unlabeled commands, or placeholder text. Validate Browser facing changes also require keyboard, axe, no console, responsive, and supported browser coverage. Use the validation and test guide /contributing/testing to run the focused and final gates.

title: Monorepo architecture
description: Locate applications, packages, contract sources, durable workflows, and the public/private repository boundary.
body: The Bun/Turbo workspace contains runtime applications under apps/ and reusable or service packages under packages/ . Runtime applications apps/admin dashboard is the authenticated operator UI. apps/checkout is buyer facing checkout/public event behavior. apps/docs builds this documentation. SDK demo apps are executable contract fixtures. Backend boundaries packages/domain owns pure rules and types. packages/db owns Kysely repositories/migrations. packages/api owns Fastify routes, auth, permissions, and serialization. packages/workflows owns Temporal workflows/activities. packages/openapi owns the public HTTP schema. Frontend and integration packages Content packages own shared editors/rendering; admin table core owns reusable table behavior; SDK and widget packages expose public integration surfaces. packages/docs core owns documentation route/help/readiness/search contracts without importing applications. Repository boundary The accepted target makes the public tixkit/tixkit repository authoritative for shared product code, public integrations, documentation, and the complete Self Hosted runtime. The private tixkit/tixkit cloud repository consumes immutable public releases and contains proprietary Cloud operations, managed integrations, and natural language agent orchestration. Public source and CI never depend on private source. During the C 130 cutover, scripts/export oss.mjs remains a temporary extraction and leak validation tool. It is not the long term publication architecture.

title: Event page Puck contract
description: Preserve one canonical Puck document across organizer authoring and public checkout rendering.
body: Event pages use one hard cutover contract. Schema v2 is Puck only content and uses @puckeditor/core terminology: Config , Data , root props, content , zones , , and . Shared imports Use @tixkit/content event page/puck for the server safe contract, validation guards, migration signatures, and Puck data aliases. Use @tixkit/content event page react/puck for the React side Puck configuration and render wrapper. EventPageDocumentV2 stores canonical Puck data at editor.data with editor.provider: "@puckeditor/core" . It never stores the former TipTap editor.document , typed blocks store, server rendered HTML, headless blocks, or a renderModel . Public payload Public checkout consumes PublicEventPagePayloadV2.page.puckData . The payload keeps document and version metadata, discovery data, settings, and the shared validation shape. The following former runtime fields are not part of the v2 payload: page.html ; page.text ; page.headless ; page.renderModel ; version.renderedHtml ; version.renderedText ; and public contentJson . Responsibility boundary Checkout Form remains the checkout data collection editor. Event Page owns the complete Puck page composition, including editable header, ticket, product add on, resale, checkout CTA, and footer blocks. Public checkout supplies live runtime data and interaction handlers to those blocks. It does not inject a second visual chrome outside the Puck document. Event media references The editor stores event owned poster, cover, and social selections as portable, event relative references: tixkit:event media:poster tixkit:event media:cover tixkit:event media:social References contain no tenant, event, rendition, host, artifact, or credential identifier. They are valid only in image bearing event page fields: root and discovery cover/social images, plus the top level imageUrl of EventHeader , EventDescription , and Media . General links, logos, speakers, sponsors, and buttons continue to require safe URLs and reject media references. Organizer previews fetch the authenticated page rendition and use a short lived object URL in memory. Saved documents retain the logical reference. Public reads resolve a copy of the published document to the exact selected role and surface page or social without rewriting the stored version. Publishing fails closed when the selected asset or required rendition is unavailable. Portable bundles preserve logical references inside versioned content documents. Import rebinding therefore resolves them against destination owned event media; private upload identifiers, signed URLs, and preview object URLs never cross the boundary. Component identifiers The v2 guards accept canonical PascalCase component types such as EventHeader , Tickets , ProductAddOns , ResaleTickets , CheckoutCta , and BrandFooter . Legacy snake case commerce types such as event header , tickets , products , resale tickets , and brand footer must fail validation after migration. Any schema or payload change requires migration coverage, admin and checkout rendering parity tests, generated contract updates, and a documented compatibility transition.

title: Set up the repository
description: Clone Tixkit, install the pinned workspace, start the stack, and run focused validation without hidden assumptions.
body: Clone the repository, enter its root, and preserve any existing working tree changes before editing. The quickstart remains in the foreground and starts infrastructure, migrations, API, worker, checkout, admin, docs, and sample data. Use a second terminal for focused tests. Work safely Read AGENTS.md , the relevant package README, and canonical guide before changing a contract. Use Graphify for cross package navigation and Serena or focused source inspection for exact symbols. Preserve unrelated dirty worktree changes; never reset or reformat them to simplify a task. Keep API, OpenAPI, SDKs, dashboard types, examples, docs, and tests synchronized in one change. Stop the foreground quickstart with Control C and verify its managed processes exit. Continue by adding documentation /contributing/add documentation through the canonical public content workflow.

title: Run validation and tests
description: Choose focused gates during implementation and execute the complete contract-sensitive suite before release.
body: Run the smallest relevant typecheck, lint, and test while iterating. Broaden validation whenever a change crosses a contract boundary. Database/provider/browser suites may require environment or infrastructure described by their package and runbook. A skipped suite is not a pass. Turbo cache output is useful during iteration, but final evidence must match the required fresh/environment backed scope. Do not weaken or delete a test to obtain green output. Fix warnings caused by the change and run git diff check plus graphify update . after code edits.

title: Authenticate API requests
description: Choose a Clerk token, scoped API key, or scanner credential and keep secrets on the correct runtime boundary.
body: Tixkit supports authenticated dashboard users, API keys, and scanner device credentials. Anonymous access is limited to explicitly public buyer routes. API keys API keys begin with tk and are bearer credentials. Creation returns the raw secret once; persistence stores a hash. Store the secret immediately in a server side secret manager. Revoked or expired keys return 401 UNAUTHORIZED . Never put the key in a query string, client bundle, mobile application package, analytics field, screenshot, or committed environment file. Clerk sessions The admin dashboard sends a Clerk session JWT. The API verifies it and resolves the active organization/tenant context. Integrations should not scrape or persist dashboard session tokens as API keys. Scanner devices Scanner devices use the issued device ID and secret headers and carry explicit check in scopes. Revoke a lost device. Do not share one device secret across an uncontrolled fleet. If a credential leaks, revoke it first, then remove it from logs/history and rotate downstream configuration.

title: Handle API errors and retries
description: Interpret the common error envelope and retry only operations that are safe to repeat.
body: Non success responses use an error object with a machine readable code , safe message, and requestId . Validation errors may include field details. Decide whether to retry Fix the request for 400 validation errors. Refresh or replace credentials for 401 only after identifying the credential issue. Correct permission/resource scope for 403 ; repeated retries will not add permission. Treat 404 as absent or inaccessible without probing adjacent identifiers. For 409 or 422 state/idempotency conflicts, reconcile the original operation before changing the request. Back off for 429 and respect any retry information. Retry transient 5xx responses only with an idempotency key where the operation requires one. Preserve safe diagnostics Log status, error code, operation ID, request ID, and a redacted local correlation ID. Do not log authorization headers, webhook secrets, full request/response payloads, ticket codes, or customer personal data.

title: Make writes idempotent
description: Prevent repeated side effects when retrying workflow, payment, inventory, ticket, message, and export mutations.
body: Generate a unique Idempotency Key for one logical mutation and retain it until that mutation reaches a known result. Reusing a key with the same payload can replay the stored result without repeating side effects. Reusing it with a different payload returns IDEMPOTENCY CONFLICT . Never use one constant key for all requests. After a timeout, query the resource or retry with the same key and identical payload. Do not generate a new key until you know the original operation should be a separate side effect.

title: API fundamentals
description: Use Tixkit's versioned JSON API with explicit authentication, scopes, pagination, errors, and idempotency.
body: Use the exact HTTPS API origin assigned to your environment, followed by the documented /v1 prefix. Hosted private beta invitations supply this origin; public documentation intentionally provides no default hosted hostname. Request model Send and accept JSON unless an operation documents a file response. Authenticated routes accept a Clerk bearer token, API key, or supported device credential according to the operation. Public buyer routes explicitly omit authentication. Every authenticated resource read is still tenant , organization , brand , or event scoped. Knowing an identifier is not sufficient authorization. Integration rules Keep secret API keys in a server secret store and send them only in the Authorization header. Use cursor pagination instead of guessing offsets. Preserve requestId from error responses for diagnosis, but never log credentials or payloads containing personal data. Supply a unique idempotency key for a mutation that moves money, inventory, tickets, messages, or durable work. Retry only according to the returned status and documented operation behavior. Contract source The API reference /reference/api is generated from packages/openapi . Conceptual guides explain safe usage; they do not duplicate an endpoint inventory. Next step Make the first API call /getting started/first api call , then configure webhook signature verification /developers/webhooks/verify signatures .

title: Paginate list operations
description: Traverse stable cursor-based pages without constructing or persisting opaque cursor values.
body: List operations use an opaque cursor with a bounded limit . A response contains items , nextCursor , and hasMore . Traverse pages Request the first page without a cursor. When hasMore is true, pass the returned nextCursor unchanged to the next request. Stop when hasMore is false and nextCursor is null. Do not decode, increment, combine, or reuse a cursor for a different endpoint/filter set. If the underlying collection changes during traversal, design the integration to tolerate repeated or newly inserted records according to the operation's ordering contract.

title: API permissions and scopes
description: Grant API keys and principals only the product capabilities and resource scope they require.
body: Authenticated principals carry product scopes such as events.read , events.write , tickets.write , orders.read , orders.write , refunds.write , attendees.read , attendees.write , checkins.read , checkins.write , box office.write , messages.write , reports.read , settings.write , developers.write , and billing.write . Least privilege Create a read only key for a read only integration. Add write or refund scopes only when the service performs those actions. A creator cannot grant scopes they do not hold. Brand or event scoped principals must create credentials within that boundary. A scope grants a capability; it does not remove tenant, organization, brand, or event isolation. Failure behavior 401 UNAUTHORIZED means the credential could not authenticate. 403 FORBIDDEN means authentication succeeded but capability or resource scope is insufficient. 404 NOT FOUND may intentionally avoid revealing an out of scope resource. Do not broaden a key before confirming which exact operation and resource boundary failed.

title: Configure a webhook endpoint
description: Register an HTTPS receiver, subscribe to explicit event types, and store the one-time signing secret safely.
body: Open Developer → Webhooks and create an endpoint with its exact HTTPS URL and only the event types the integration handles. Store the secret once Endpoint creation returns a signing secret once. Move it directly to the receiving service's secret manager. Do not copy it into a URL, browser storage, analytics, screenshots, issue reports, or committed configuration. To rotate, create or activate the replacement secret/endpoint according to the supported dashboard flow, deploy verification, validate delivery, and disable the old endpoint. Do not disable the working path before the replacement verifies successfully. Return promptly Read the raw body, verify signature and timestamp, durably record the event ID, and return a 2xx response promptly. Perform slow business work asynchronously. Non 2xx responses and delivery failures are retried; repeated processing must be idempotent. Verify configuration Send a test delivery, confirm a successful status in Tixkit, and reconcile the event ID in receiver logs without recording the secret or full sensitive payload.

title: Test webhook delivery
description: Exercise local forwarding, signature failure, retry, duplicate delivery, and successful processing without production data.
body: Use test events and a development endpoint. Do not forward production payloads into local logs or tunneling services. Inspect the forwarding plan The dry run reports the planned target without starting Stripe CLI or writing a secret. Live provider forwarding requires the supported provider CLI and test credentials in the selected environment file. Exercise receiver behavior 1. Deliver a correctly signed event and return 2xx only after durable acceptance. 2. Change one body byte and verify the signature is rejected. 3. Use a stale timestamp and verify replay protection rejects it. 4. Return a non 2xx response and observe retry state. 5. Deliver the same event ID twice and verify business work happens once. 6. Restore success and confirm delivery status in the Developer dashboard. Do not log the Authorization header, endpoint secret, or full personal data payload while testing.

title: Troubleshoot webhook delivery
description: Diagnose endpoint, signature, response, retry, dead-letter, and replay failures from observable state.
body: Start with the last delivery status, attempt count, safe response summary, and event ID. Do not rotate secrets or replay until the failure category is known. Endpoint was not reached Verify HTTPS URL, DNS, TLS, firewall, and receiver availability. Confirm the endpoint is active and subscribed to the event type. Signature verification failed Confirm the receiver uses the raw body, current endpoint secret, t and v1 fields, hex decoding, constant time comparison, and a synchronized clock. Parsing then reserializing JSON changes the signed bytes. Receiver returned non 2xx Inspect the receiver's redacted error using the event ID. Fix durable acceptance or downstream queueing before replay. A slow synchronous handler may time out even if it eventually performs work. Delivery is dead lettered After retry attempts are exhausted, correct the endpoint first. Replay only when the receiver is idempotent and the operator understands the downstream effect. Replaying financial or fulfillment events without deduplication can repeat side effects.

title: Verify webhook signatures
description: Authenticate the raw request body with HMAC-SHA256, constant-time comparison, and timestamp tolerance.
body: The X Tixkit Signature header contains t= ,v1= . Tixkit signs ${timestamp}.${rawBody} with HMAC SHA256. Verify before parsing Compute the digest before JSON parsing or reserialization. Reject missing, malformed, stale, or mismatched signatures. Use constant time comparison and keep the endpoint secret out of error messages. Prevent replay Timestamp tolerance limits stale requests but does not deduplicate valid retries. Store the stable webhook event ID and make processing idempotent. A delivery attempt ID may change across attempts; the event ID identifies the logical event. Continue with the generated API reference /reference/api and a supported SDK guide /sdks/javascript after the verification fixture passes.

title: Embed Tixkit checkout
description: Choose inline, modal, button, or redirect integration and generate CSP-aware markup without exposing secrets.
body: The widget is a browser integration and must use public event/brand identifiers only. API keys and provider secrets never belong in embed markup. Generate a reviewed snippet The CLI prints the snippet, CSP guidance, and placement instructions. Review generated origins against your actual deployment; do not copy default hosted domains into a self hosted policy without changing them. The current production release is immutable and integrity pinned: Use bun run embed:generate instead of editing the release URL or integrity value by hand. The release pin validation fails when this public example drifts from the widget manifest. Choose a mode Inline reserves content space and keeps checkout visible in the page flow. Modal opens an overlay and must preserve focus and escape behavior. Button defers loading until user intent. Redirect navigates to hosted checkout and is the simplest isolation boundary. Test keyboard operation, mobile width, CSP enforcement, lifecycle callbacks, and return navigation. Tracking identifiers must be non personal attribution values.

title: Choose a deployment model
description: Choose between Tixkit Cloud, its hosted Platform API capability, local evaluation, and Self-Hosted operation.
body: Tixkit's accepted product model includes Tixkit Cloud, the hosted Platform API capability inside Cloud, and Tixkit Self Hosted over one shared product. Cloud and the managed agent layer remain experimental/private beta plans until their provisioning, operations, support, security, and release gates are complete; this page does not claim general availability before then. Tixkit Cloud Choose Cloud when Tixkit should operate upgrades, workflows, storage, monitoring, backups, security maintenance, hosted admin, event pages, checkout, and delivery. Platform API customers use this same hosted backend with more control through APIs, SDKs, widgets, headless checkout, OAuth, scoped keys, webhooks, and custom product UI. Local evaluation Choose the local stack when you need to evaluate workflows, develop an integration, or contribute. Docker Compose starts PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, Temporal, and MinIO. The CLI then runs migrations and starts the API, worker, checkout, admin, and documentation applications. Local capture mode payments record platform behavior without contacting a payment provider. They are not a substitute for provider validation. Self hosted operation Choose self hosting when your team can operate: a supported relational database configuration; Redis, Temporal, and object storage; API and worker processes with health monitoring; public admin, checkout, and documentation applications; TLS, secrets, backups, restore rehearsals, upgrades, and incident response. Provider backed payments, messaging, and authentication require their documented credentials and provider side setup. Do not copy local example values into production. Decision check Use local evaluation until you can complete a test event, test checkout, API request, webhook verification, backup, and restore rehearsal. Move to a production topology only after the deployment guide /self hosting/deployment and incident runbooks /operations/incidents match your environment.

title: Make the first API call
description: Create a narrowly scoped server-only key and use it for a non-destructive request.
body: Tixkit API keys are secrets for server side use. Do not paste a secret into browser code, a URL, documentation feedback, analytics, screenshots, or persistent browser storage. Create a scoped key Open Developer → API keys in the admin dashboard. Create a key with only the read scope needed to list events. Copy the secret from the one time display directly into your server secret manager or current shell, then dismiss it. Tixkit does not display the secret again. Paste the secret only at the silent prompt; the value is not part of the recorded command. Clear the variable with unset TIXKIT API KEY when the session ends. Do not add it to shell history, committed .env files, command arguments, or client visible NEXT PUBLIC variables. List events safely config reads the expanded header from standard input, so the secret is not placed in curl's process arguments or a temporary file. A successful response is JSON containing the events visible to the key's tenant and scope. An empty list is a valid result. Diagnose failures 401 Unauthorized: the header is missing, malformed, expired, revoked, or contains the wrong key. 403 Forbidden: authentication succeeded but the key lacks the required scope or tenant access. 404 Not Found: verify the assigned origin, /v1 base path, and environment. Connection failure: confirm the assigned API origin and environment status before rotating the key. Rotate or revoke the key immediately if it was copied into a browser, URL, log, screenshot, or committed file. Continue with webhook signature verification /developers/webhooks/verify signatures , authentication and key handling /developers/api fundamentals/authentication , or the generated API reference /reference/api .

title: Create and publish the first event
description: Configure an event, schedule, sellable inventory, checkout form, preview, and publication state.
body: This path creates a test event that can reach checkout. Publishing an event without sellable inventory or a valid schedule does not create a usable buyer flow. Create the event 1. Open Events in the admin dashboard and choose Create event . 2. Enter a test safe name, description, venue or online context, and the organization/brand requested by the form. 3. Save the event before adding child resources. The event detail page must load without a scope or permission error. If it does not, confirm the selected organization and brand rather than recreating the event in another tenant. Configure schedule and inventory Add at least one occurrence with a future start time. Then create a ticket type or product with a positive price, available quantity, and sales window that includes the current time. Verify the inventory view shows a sellable item. A draft item, zero capacity, expired sales window, or inactive product is not available at checkout. Review checkout behavior Open the checkout form editor. Review required buyer and attendee fields, consent text, and fee presentation. Save the current revision. Use only test safe wording and data. Preview before publishing Open the public event or checkout preview from the event action. Confirm the correct brand, schedule, item, price, and required form fields. Return to the dashboard and publish the event only after the preview matches the intended test workflow. Verify publication Reload the event detail page and confirm the status is published. Then open the public event page in a private browser window. If the event is missing, inspect schedule, sales window, domain, and inventory state before changing publication repeatedly. Next step Complete a test checkout /getting started/test checkout and keep the resulting order available for refund and check in practice.

title: Run Tixkit locally
description: Start infrastructure, migrations, applications, documentation, and sample data from a clean source checkout.
body: Run the quickstart from the root of a Tixkit source checkout. It intentionally refuses to run from an unrelated directory because it controls repository infrastructure and application processes. Install and configure setup:check exits nonzero and prints the missing or invalid fields when configuration is incomplete. Fix the reported values instead of bypassing the check. Start the stack The command checks Docker and required ports, starts local infrastructure, runs database migrations, starts the API, worker, checkout, admin, and docs applications, waits for their health checks, and seeds idempotent sample data. Expected final output includes: The process remains in the foreground. Press Control C once and wait for the managed child processes to stop. Verify the result Open the admin dashboard at http://localhost:3001 , the documentation at http://localhost:3002 , and the Temporal UI at http://localhost:8080 . Verify the API directly: Each command must return a successful response. A rendered page alone does not prove the worker or database is healthy. Common failures Docker is unavailable: start Docker Desktop or the Docker daemon, then rerun the command. A required port is occupied: stop the conflicting process. Do not change one application port without updating every dependent URL. Services time out: inspect the foreground logs for the named unhealthy service, then rerun bun run setup:check mode local . Sample data fails: stop the stack, correct the API or database error, and rerun. Use skip seed only when you deliberately want an empty workspace. Next step Create the first event /getting started/first event with the seeded local principal and workspace.

title: Platform overview
description: Understand Tixkit's event-commerce boundaries before choosing an operating or integration path.

headings.text: Choose the surface for your task

body: Tixkit separates event operations from buyer checkout. Operators work in the admin dashboard; buyers use hosted or embedded checkout; integrations call the API or a supported SDK. The API applies tenant, organization, brand, and event scope before repositories read or change data. Choose the surface for your task Use the admin dashboard to configure workspaces, events, inventory, checkout forms, orders, attendees, messages, and reports. Use the hosted checkout or widget for buyer facing purchase flows. Use the API and SDKs for server side integrations and scanner workflows. Self hosters operate the API, worker, database, Redis, Temporal, object storage, admin, checkout, and documentation surfaces. A local capture payment mode is useful for development, but it is not proof that a production payment provider is ready. Contract boundaries packages/domain owns pure business types and rules. packages/db owns Kysely repositories, database types, and migrations. packages/api owns authentication, authorization, serialization, and HTTP routes. packages/openapi owns the public HTTP contract used for reference generation and SDK parity. packages/workflows owns durable Temporal workflows and activities. apps/admin dashboard and apps/checkout consume those contracts; they do not define backend truth. Support labels Every guide identifies its stability. Stable describes a supported contract covered by validation. Beta means the workflow exists but may still change before a stable release. Experimental behavior must not be treated as production ready. Environment specific capture or mock behavior is labeled where it appears. Next step Choose a deployment model /getting started/deployment model if you are evaluating Tixkit, or run Tixkit locally /getting started/local quickstart if you are ready to inspect the complete stack.

title: Complete a test checkout
description: Verify buyer checkout and the resulting order without treating capture-mode behavior as provider readiness.
body: Use test only attendee and buyer data. Never place a real payment credential into a test environment or documentation example. Confirm the payment mode Use only the test payment mode assigned to the environment. Confirm the payment account status in workspace settings before checkout. A successful test order proves the configured test journey; it does not by itself prove that live payments, settlement, disputes, or refunds are ready. Complete the purchase 1. Open the published event in a private browser window. 2. Select one available test ticket or product. 3. Complete all required buyer, attendee, and consent fields with non customer data. 4. Review quantity, fees, discounts, and total before confirming. 5. Complete the environment appropriate payment step. Do not refresh or submit repeatedly while confirmation is pending. The flow uses idempotency and durable processing, but duplicate user actions complicate diagnosis. Verify the order Return to Orders in the admin dashboard. Find the new order and confirm its payment/order state, line items, attendee records, and total. If checkout showed success but no order appears, preserve the non secret order/session identifier and use the environment's authorized diagnostics or support channel. Prepare downstream operations Use the test order to practice refund handling /operators/orders/refunds and check in /operators/check in . Refunds may have external side effects; use only the environment's documented test mode for rehearsal.

title: Incident runbooks
description: Triage and recover payment, refund, webhook, checkout-workflow, export, and worker incidents.
body: Protect buyers and preserve evidence before changing state. Record severity, start time, affected environment, safe correlation identifiers, and the current mitigation owner. Never paste secrets, credentials, customer payloads, or raw database dumps into the incident record. General triage 1. Confirm scope by tenant/organization/brand/event without crossing isolation boundaries. 2. Check recent deploys, migrations, provider status, API/worker health, task queue lag, database, Redis, and storage. 3. Stop or rate limit the unsafe side effect while preserving read access where possible. 4. Choose rollback, forward repair, provider reconciliation, or restore based on tested compatibility. Payment or refund disagreement Reconcile Tixkit order/refund records, workflow history, and provider references. Do not issue a second refund or capture before confirming the first attempt. Use the supported compensation/repair path and verify customer facing status afterward. Webhook dead letters Confirm endpoint reachability and signature verification, then fix receiver idempotency before replay. Replay a bounded event set and verify event IDs at the receiver. Stuck checkout or export Inspect the durable workflow/activity and dependency status. Restore workers/storage/providers, retry through supported operations, and verify order/inventory or export artifact state. Avoid creating many duplicate jobs. Recovery validation Run targeted health and golden path checks, confirm alerts clear for the right reason, communicate residual impact, and capture follow up changes with owners. Rehearse restore when integrity is uncertain.

title: Operate Temporal workflows
description: Deploy workers, monitor task queues, preserve replay safety, and recover stuck durable operations.
body: Tixkit uses Temporal for durable checkout, refund, webhook delivery, exports, and other asynchronous operations. The API may accept a request before every activity completes; workflow state is part of operational truth. Deploy workers Deploy workers with the same task queue, namespace, connection, encryption/TLS, and compatible application contract as the API. Verify worker readiness only after required recovery schedulers and registrations are established. Preserve replay safety Workflow code must remain deterministic. Do not add direct network, clock, random, database, or environment dependent behavior inside workflow execution; place side effects in activities. Use Temporal versioning patterns before changing an existing workflow branch that may replay. Diagnose a stuck workflow 1. Identify the workflow ID and type without copying payloads into public channels. 2. Inspect history, pending activity, attempt, timeout, and task queue polling. 3. Restore the missing dependency or worker before retrying. 4. Use supported reset/retry/repair behavior only after understanding idempotency and side effects. 5. Verify the associated order, payment, inventory, delivery, or export state—not only workflow closure. Never delete workflow history or mutate application rows to make a dashboard look complete.

title: Manage attendees
description: Find attendee records, understand admission state, and protect ticket-bearing personal data.
body: Attendee records connect order line items to admission. They may contain personal data and ticket codes, so expose only the minimum information needed for an authorized task. Find an attendee Use the event and attendee views in the correct organization/brand context. Search by an authorized identifier and confirm the related event and order before changing state. Understand status An attendee can exist before check in and can have ticket or delivery state distinct from the parent order. A paid order does not mean every attendee has been admitted; a checked in attendee must not be admitted again without an explicit supervised correction. Resolve a lookup problem If the attendee is absent, confirm the event scope, order completion, attendee form answers, and whether the purchase created multiple attendees. For door operations, use the documented manual lookup rather than sharing raw ticket codes between devices. Prepare staff and devices with the check in guide /operators/check in .

title: Run box office and point-of-sale orders
description: Create supervised event orders while preserving inventory, payment-mode, and permission boundaries.
body: Box office orders use the same event and inventory boundaries as buyer checkout, with operator controlled entry and payment context. Confirm the sale context Verify organization, brand, event, occurrence, currency, and payment mode before adding items. Confirm the operator is authorized for box office writes; order read permission alone is insufficient. Create the order Select only currently available items, enter the minimum required buyer/attendee information, and review totals and fees. Submit once and wait for the order result. In provider backed environments, follow the approved terminal or payment workflow rather than entering card data into an unsupported field. Verify and hand off Open the resulting order and attendee records. Confirm the intended fulfillment or ticket delivery state before telling the buyer the sale is complete. If creation fails, retain the non secret attempt reference and check inventory/payment state before retrying.

title: Configure brands and domains
description: Manage customer-facing identity and verify that brand changes reach public surfaces.
body: A brand controls customer facing identity within an organization. Treat domain verification, sender identity, and visual branding as separate readiness signals; changing a logo does not verify a domain or messaging provider. Update visual identity Open Settings → Branding for the selected brand. Use organization approved names, colors, and public assets. Preview light and dark contexts where the dashboard provides them, then save and reload. Use assets that contain no customer data, credentials, or internal environment details. Keep critical instructions in text; a logo or screenshot must not be the only way to understand a flow. Verify the public result Open a published test event or checkout preview in a private browser window. Confirm the expected brand, not merely the admin preview. Cached public content may require a new revision or refresh according to the current editor workflow. Resolve common blockers A missing public logo usually means the asset was not saved, the wrong brand is selected, or the public revision has not incorporated the change. A custom domain is not ready until its verification status is authoritative; DNS edits alone are not completion. Email sender readiness is provider specific and separate from brand display settings. Next, create and configure an event /operators/events .

title: Prepare and run check-in
description: Configure authorized devices, validate scans, and use safe offline or manual fallbacks.
body: Rehearse check in with test tickets before doors open. Confirm device authentication, event scope, connectivity expectations, and the manual fallback path. Prepare the station Select the event and verify the scanner contract/configuration shown by the dashboard. Authorize only the devices and staff that need admission access. Do not place device secrets in URLs, shared notes, screenshots, or analytics. Run a test scan for a valid ticket, a duplicate scan, an invalid code, and a ticket from another event. The UI must clearly distinguish each result without exposing raw internal errors. Operate at the door Keep the camera permission and event scope visible. After a successful admission, wait for confirmation before scanning the next code. Use manual lookup only when the attendee can be verified through the authorized workflow. Offline behavior Use offline manifests only when the configured scanner flow supports them. Verify manifest signature and freshness; reconnect and synchronize as soon as practical. Offline acceptance is not permission to bypass event scope or admit a duplicate without review. If a ticket fails, identify whether it is unknown, wrong event, already used, stale/offline, or blocked by device authorization before escalating.

title: Operate events
description: Understand event state, schedules, inventory, previews, and publication dependencies.
body: The Events area is the operating hub for schedules, sellable items, checkout fields, messaging, marketing, and public presentation. Event publication is a state transition, not proof that every downstream dependency is ready. Work in dependency order 1. Confirm organization and brand context. 2. Create the event and save its core details. 3. Add a valid schedule or occurrence. 4. Add sellable ticket or product inventory. 5. Review checkout fields, consent, fees, and payment readiness. 6. Preview the public experience. 7. Publish and verify from a private browser window. Understand event status Draft events are editable but not expected to appear as a live public sale. Published events still depend on active schedules, sale windows, inventory, public revisions, brand/domain context, and payment behavior. If an event cannot be published, resolve the exact prerequisite shown by the dashboard. Do not repeatedly toggle status or duplicate the event to work around a missing dependency. Protect scoped data Event URLs and identifiers are not authorization. The API and dashboard must enforce tenant, organization, brand, and event access for every read and write. Report any cross context data immediately through the security process. Use schedules /operators/events/schedules , tickets and products /operators/events/tickets and products , and checkout forms /operators/events/checkout forms to complete the setup.

title: Configure checkout forms and consent
description: Collect only necessary buyer and attendee data and verify the active public revision.
body: Checkout forms can collect buyer level and attendee level answers. Minimize personal data and make required fields and consent language explicit. Review the form Open the event checkout form view. For each field, confirm its audience, requirement state, label, and purpose. Use attendee fields only when the answer must differ per admission; use buyer fields for order level contact or agreement. Do not request credentials, payment card data, government identifiers, or unrelated sensitive information in custom fields. Save and preview Save the form revision, then open checkout preview. Add more than one ticket when validating attendee level behavior. Confirm required validation, accessible labels, error text, consent presentation, and the final order summary. Diagnose stale behavior If checkout shows an older form, verify the correct event and brand, the saved/public revision, and whether an existing checkout session captured an earlier revision. Start a new private session before assuming the save failed. Complete a test checkout /getting started/test checkout after every material form or consent change.

title: Configure event schedules
description: Add occurrences that make event timing explicit for buyers and operators.
body: Schedules determine when an event occurs and provide context for checkout, attendee operations, and reporting. Add an occurrence Open the event schedule view and add a future start time with the intended timezone and any supported end or door time. Save, reload, and verify the displayed local time. Timezone errors are operationally expensive. Confirm the venue timezone and do not infer it from the operator's browser. When daylight saving boundaries are relevant, verify the exact rendered date and offset. Change an active schedule safely Before changing an event that already has orders, determine how the change affects buyer communication, tickets, check in, and integrations. Save the new value once, verify it on the public event page, and use the messaging workflow when attendees must be notified. Troubleshoot If a published event is missing from public discovery, confirm that at least one occurrence is active and that its timing, publication, sales window, and brand context are compatible. A schedule alone does not override inactive inventory. Continue with sellable inventory /operators/events/tickets and products .

title: Configure tickets, products, and inventory
description: Create sellable items with explicit capacity, pricing, availability, and sale windows.
body: An item is sellable only when its status, price, capacity, inventory pool, and sales window permit a purchase. Public availability is authoritative; an item appearing in the admin editor is not sufficient. Create a ticket or product Open the event's tickets/products view. Define a customer facing name, price and currency, capacity or inventory source, and sales window. Save and reload before creating dependent rules. Use test values in non production environments. Do not use an artificial zero price to bypass payment path validation unless a free item is the intended product behavior. Verify availability Open the event preview and confirm the item is visible with the expected price and remaining availability. If it is absent, check: draft or inactive status; zero or exhausted inventory; sales window not yet open or already closed; inventory pool or occurrence mismatch; access rules, promotion requirements, or public revision state. Avoid oversell assumptions Checkout uses holds and durable confirmation behavior. Do not infer capacity from the count displayed in one browser or manually change database rows. Use supported admin/API operations and verify the resulting public availability. Next, review checkout fields and consent /operators/events/checkout forms .

title: Configure and send messages
description: Work with lifecycle and campaign content while respecting sender verification, consent, and delivery evidence.
body: The content editor, sender identity, audience selection, and transport status are separate controls. A saved template is not proof of provider delivery. Prepare content Select the correct brand and event scope. Use the lifecycle or campaign editor appropriate to the message. Preview content with test data and confirm links, unsubscribe/consent behavior, and accessible structure. Verify sender readiness Provider delivery requires the environment's verified email or SMS sender configuration. Local capture behavior can validate rendering without proving provider acceptance. Resolve sender warnings before a live send. Send and verify Use a limited test audience first. Confirm the dashboard's delivery/capture state and, when authorized, provider evidence. Do not copy recipient lists, message bodies containing personal data, or provider credentials into support reports. If delivery fails, distinguish invalid sender, provider rejection, transport error, recipient status, and template/render failure before retrying.

title: Operate durable migrations
description: Dry-run, commit, recover, reconcile, and safely correct tenant migration jobs.
body: Tixkit migrations are durable, tenant scoped jobs. Treat the job report—not an adapter log—as the source of truth for dry run readiness, progress, and conflicts. Treat the live rollback assessment as the source of truth for rollback eligibility. Migration workers may retry a chunk; adapters and the core therefore use stable external references and idempotent writes. Operator lifecycle 1. Upload source objects with upload purpose migration import and wait for a clean malware scan result. Retain the returned opaque uploadArtifactId . 2. For an official API source, register an expiring source credential reference. Then create the job with its source system, adapter version, mapping profile, timezone, currency assumptions, and credential ID when that source mode requires one. Portable and file export jobs do not use a source credential. 3. Register each clean uploadArtifactId on the job. Tixkit derives storage metadata and checksums; clients never submit object keys or asserted hashes. 4. Save or select mappings, then run the dry run. Resolve every fatal/error issue and review warnings, unsupported features, duplicates, mapping failures, counts, and runtime/storage estimates. 5. Save the final report and approval evidence. Confirm that its input/configuration hashes still match the job. 6. Commit using the exact job bound acknowledgement. Monitor durable progress events and reconciliation metrics. 7. Activate imported entities only after reconciliation. Keep source files and reports under the configured retention policy. Never skip directly from creation to commit. The API rejects a stale or unsuccessful dry run even if a client attempts it. Migration imports use an organization scoped upload artifact. organizationId is required for migration import and rejected for every other upload purpose; brandId and eventId are not allowed on migration uploads. Each artifact must be no larger than 50 MiB. Portable bundles must use the exact application/vnd.tixkit.portable+json media type; generic migration adapters retain their documented source media types. Upload the exact bytes to the returned short lived URL, then call the artifact completion endpoint and wait for a clean scan result before registering it on a job. Registration is single use and atomically links the artifact to the job, records consumption, and starts a 30 day retention window. Tixkit renews recently active preparation, commit, cancellation, and rollback work in one day increments, with a 90 day absolute ceiling. Pending, ready, committed, failed, paused, terminal, and inactive jobs do not renew automatically. Unregistered clean artifacts expire with their upload ticket. Inconsistent consumed artifact linkage is placed on retention hold instead of deleting bytes. Preparation start/resume and commit atomically acquire the exact artifact lease before the job becomes active. If cleanup already acquired the artifact, the lifecycle action fails without changing job state; if the lifecycle action acquired it first, cleanup cannot delete it. A bundle at the 90 day ceiling cannot enter preparation or commit; create and approve a fresh export instead. Retain the source export independently through destination activation and any longer policy your organization requires. JavaScript SDK workflow @tixkit/js exposes every public migration route through client.migrations . Its create input is a discriminated union: sourceSystem must match configuration.sourceSystem , official API sources require their documented selectors and credentialId , and export jobs accept only upload artifact IDs. The typed mapping methods are createMapping and mappings ; report retrieval is available as both report and downloadReport . SDK methods apply the same tenant permissions, confirmation headers, and server side validation as direct HTTP calls. Tixkit portable bundle imports Create the initial configuration snapshot with POST /v1/portable exports . After source data changes, create a signed successor with POST /v1/portable delta exports , passing the completed parent job as parentExportJobId . The source reopens the immutable parent bytes, verifies their checksum, signature and internal lineage, then binds the exact parent bundle, manifest hash and cursor into the successor. Sequence numbers increase but may contain gaps after failed builds; the signed parent tuple is authoritative. For the final successor after write freeze, include cutoverFreeze.frozenAt and the SHA 256 of the source freeze receipt. This receipt hash is a signed manifest commitment; destination commit authorization still depends on its separately validated, short lived signed PortableCutoverProof . Both export endpoints require Idempotency Key ; changing a parent or freeze receipt under the same key is an idempotency conflict. Retain every exported artifact through destination activation because each delta embeds and verifies its immediate signed parent, and keep the bundle signing key pinned for the full chain because key rotation between parent and successor is not currently supported. Activating the final delta permanently closes that destination lineage: subsequent deltas and implicit full snapshot rebaselines fail closed. These cutover deltas are finite state reconciliation snapshots, not continuous active active replication. Use the tixkit portable adapter for the signed logical bundle transport. A portable job accepts exactly one clean migration import artifact and does not use a source credential. The artifact is a strict JSON object containing the signed envelope and a payloads object whose keys are manifest paths and whose values are canonical base64. A delta artifact must also contain the exact signed parentEnvelope ; full artifacts must omit it. The worker verifies the outer upload checksum, current and parent manifest signatures, exact delta cursor lineage, payload/media attestations, decoded bytes, compatibility, destination scope, counts, and canonical entity shape before staging any row. Configure TIXKIT PORTABILITY IMPORT TRUST on workers with the destination compatibility contract, Ed25519 public verification keys, and exact payload/media policy identities. The registry is closed and fail closed: unknown fields, private key algorithms, string shaped allowlists, duplicate allowlist entries, unbound policy keys, and malformed versions are rejected at worker startup/use. Rotate verification keys by overlapping trusted public keys; every resumed chunk reloads trust and re verifies the immutable artifact. The importer restores owned event poster, cover, and social assets alongside logical configuration. Export normalizes each clean owned original to metadata stripped WebP, binds its checksum and event role into the signed manifest, and includes a signed media safety attestation. Import reopens the exact registered bundle at commit time, verifies its artifact and preflight evidence, decodes WebP under the 40 million pixel limit, and writes checksum addressed destination storage before creating scoped media records. Media bytes are never copied into migration provenance rows. Failed, replaced, or rolled back object writes use durable cleanup jobs processed by Temporal maintenance with reference checks and retry backoff. Trust registries for bundles that contain event media must include tixkit event media scanner v1 in mediaPolicies , allow only image/webp , and bind that policy to the public Ed25519 key matching the export payload signing key. Current exports require data schema 0081 and capabilities portable bundle v2 , portable rebinding kinds v2 , and portable content documents v1 ; destinations must declare the exact schema and all three capabilities. Schema 0081 carries event page, email, and SMS content documents through the signed logical bundle. iMessage and social invite documents are excluded until their public, versioned channel contracts are available; a bundle containing either channel fails policy validation instead of silently dropping it. Imported content versions are always restored as drafts: source publication timestamps and publication pointers are intentionally omitted, and an organizer must review and publish at the destination. Keep C 127 open until Cloud → Self Hosted, Self Hosted → Cloud, and Self Hosted → Self Hosted hosted round trips are recorded; local public implementation proof alone is not hosted availability proof. Current exports use immutable manifest schema v2 tixkit portable bundle v2 , dated 2026 07 14 and require destinations to declare both portable bundle v2 and portable rebinding kinds v2 . The original dated v1 schema remains available for verification and legacy imports; v1 validators correctly reject the new typed kinds. Rebindings are typed and cannot be substituted across payment accounts, email delivery routes, SMS delivery routes, marketing integrations, custom domains, sending identities, OAuth redirect origins, webhook endpoints, tax registrations, or wallet credentials. Active and verified source resources are required before commit; inactive or unverified resources are optional but may be bound for later activation. Tax registrations are tenant/organization scoped; wallet credentials are additionally bound to an owned brand. Their provider custody references must use an approved opaque secret manager, KMS/HSM, or cloud ARN reference without URI userinfo, query, or fragment data. Registration secrets, certificates, and private signing material stay in the source environment. Rebinding evidence contains only opaque source and destination resource identifiers—never credentials, provider account IDs, endpoint URLs, signing material, or secret configuration. Portable jobs remain domain commit disabled until required destination rebindings and reconciliation are complete. A successful dry run now produces an immutable signed receipt bound to the exact staged input and source artifact. Self Hosted deployments configure PORTABILITY DRY RUN SIGNING KEY ID , PORTABILITY DRY RUN SIGNING PRIVATE KEY BASE64 , and an overlapping PORTABILITY DRY RUN TRUSTED PUBLIC KEYS keyring during rotation. Managed Cloud supplies the same public authority interface through managed key custody; public code does not require or expose Cloud private keys. Before approval, read GET /v1/migration jobs/ /portable rebindings . Bind every required source reference with PUT /v1/migration jobs/ /portable rebindings/ and a destinationReference naming an existing destination resource. These are opaque resource identifiers, not URLs, credentials, tokens, connection strings, or private keys. Unknown manifest references and secret bearing values are rejected. Each binding records deterministic provenance and an audit event. An operator with migrations.commit must then approve that exact receipt with Idempotency Key and x tixkit confirmation: approve: : . The returned commit confirmation binds the principal, tenant, organization, job, operation, manifest, artifact, staged input, completed destination rebindings, receipt, issue time, and ten minute expiry. Approval is immutable and revocable before execution starts. Material staging or rebinding changes invalidate approval, and expired or revoked approvals fail closed. Before the final commit request, the source control plane signs a PortableCutoverProof with the shared protocol helper. For a full bundle, the source must actually be write frozen and set sourceFrozen: true ; a delta bundle may attest the final cursor without claiming a freeze. The proof binds the source tenant, deployment and cursor; bundle and manifest; destination and operation; observed time; five minute maximum expiry; and a unique nonce. Configure the destination API with PORTABILITY CUTOVER TRUSTED PUBLIC KEYS , a JSON keyring of source Ed25519 public keys. Rotate keys with an overlap window and remove an old key only after its outstanding bundles expire. Call POST /v1/migration jobs/ /commit with the exact returned approval confirmation and body { "cutoverProof": } . The destination requires an observation no more than 60 seconds old, validates every binding and signature, and atomically stores immutable proof evidence while consuming keyId, nonce globally. Invalid, expired, cross destination, substituted, or replayed proof fails closed. Commit authorization, nonce consumption, job promotion, and execution sealing are one serialized database transition; the worker independently verifies the authorization, staged input digest, approval, and active destination resources before any domain write. Once execution starts, approval and bound resource revocation are refused so a mid stage revocation cannot race a domain write. Pause or cancel the migration at its durable chunk boundary instead. After every dependency stage completes, the workflow records reconciliation evidence and leaves the job committed . Activation is a separate consequential action. Confirm the report has zero unresolved rows, current input and rebinding digests, and the expected reconciliation event, then call POST /v1/migration jobs/ /activate with x tixkit confirmation: activate: and an empty body. The activation transaction rechecks all of those gates and active destination resources before changing the job to activated . CLI workflow Keep credentials out of command arguments and shell history: A minimal create request is: Upload source files with upload purpose migration import , complete malware scanning, then register the returned uploadArtifactId on the job. The server derives the immutable object key, size, media type, and SHA 256 from the tenant and organization scoped upload artifact; clients cannot supply an arbitrary storage key. migration:prepare starts the durable Temporal acquisition/normalization workflow. Wait for the job to reach ready before running dry run. Preparation persists bounded row chunks and opaque cursors, and can be paused, resumed, cancelled, or retried without embedding source records in job configuration. Use migration:pause , migration:resume , and migration:cancel for lifecycle control. These are requests: wait until job status confirms the durable checkpoint. Run migration:rollback assessment immediately before rollback and review eligible , mode , blockers, and any correctivePlanId . migration:rollback requires confirm 'ROLLBACK ' and still fails closed when the server detects live activity or downstream references. API key and source credential TIXKIT API KEY authenticates the operator to Tixkit. It is not the credential used to read a source system. Source credentials stay in the deployment's secret manager; Tixkit stores only an expiring reference: Never submit the raw source token, password, cookie, or authorization header in job configuration or mappings. The credential reference is organization and source scoped. Tixkit revalidates its registry expiry and secret manager availability when API preparation and commit begin. If it expires, is revoked, or no longer resolves, register a new reference, create a new job configuration, and repeat preparation and dry run; do not extend or replace committed evidence in place. Revoke a superseded reference with DELETE /v1/migration credentials/{credentialId}?organizationId={organizationId} . Self hosted workers bind accepted aws secretsmanager:// , gcp secretmanager:// , secret:// , or vault:// references to injected environment variables through TIXKIT MIGRATION CREDENTIAL BINDINGS . The JSON registry contains no secret material and must match both the complete reference and source system: Set TIXKIT MIGRATION GENERIC CSV SECRET through the deployment secret manager. Bindings must match the exact reference, tenant, organization, and source system. Public env:// references are rejected, malformed registries fail closed, and missing bindings or environment material prevent commit. Dry run guarantee A dry run may persist job control rows, uploaded file metadata, normalized staging rows, validation findings, mappings, conflicts, and progress events. It performs zero writes to live event, inventory, buyer, order, payment, ticket, or check in domains. It does not reserve inventory, send messages, deliver webhooks, fulfill tickets, or contact payment providers. Before approving commit, verify the report contains create/update/skip/conflict counts, issue severities, unsupported feature losses, duplicate and mapping findings, date/timezone/currency findings, and runtime/storage estimates. Changing any source object, adapter, mapping, or behavior affecting option invalidates the report and requires another dry run. Source object safety Use tenant and organization scoped migration import upload artifacts and short lived upload credentials. Verify content length and SHA 256 before parsing and again before commit. Reject path traversal, archives with unsafe entries or expansion ratios, unsupported encodings, and unexpected media types. Malware scan uploads where the deployment supports scanning. Quarantine rather than parse failed objects. Encrypt source objects and reports at rest. Redact secrets and unnecessary buyer PII from logs and progress events. Do not replace an object in place. A changed hash is a new input and invalidates the dry run. Apply explicit retention and deletion policies to source exports, row payloads, and reports. Historical financial records Imported payments and refunds are historical snapshots with source amount, currency, provider reference, source timestamp, and provenance. They are not proof that a Tixkit provider transaction succeeded. Migration code must never generate provider success events, settle funds, initiate refunds, create synthetic completed payments, or trigger fulfillment, notification, or webhook side effects. Reconcile snapshots explicitly against provider records when required. A reconciliation result is separate provenance; it must not rewrite the original source values silently. Amount or currency mismatches block activation until an operator records the approved correction. Cancellation, rollback, and correction Before commit, cancellation is safe and leaves live domains unchanged. During commit, cancellation takes effect at a durable chunk boundary; already committed chunks remain idempotently recorded and are reconciled before any resume or rollback decision. After commit but before activation, rollback may delete only untouched entities created by that job. It must refuse destructive rollback when an imported entity has a new sale, scan, transfer, edit, provider event, or downstream reference. Entities updated rather than created are not blindly restored. After live activity, the rollback assessment refuses deletion and persists an immutable rollback.corrective plan event. Download the report again and inspect its correctivePlans collection. Each plan identifies its event ID, blockers, impacted entities, saved mappings, and safe actions. The migration owner must attach the plan to the incident, obtain the same operational/financial approval required for the affected records, execute only additive or scoped corrections, and retain the completion evidence. Typical corrections are additive mappings, scoped edits, compensating historical snapshots, or explicit deactivation. Never delete evidence or manufacture provider history to make totals agree. Incident and recovery 1. Pause the affected job and prevent activation. Do not terminate Temporal histories or edit job state directly. 2. Capture the job ID, run/workflow ID, adapter/version, input/configuration hashes, last durable cursor, failing chunk, and redacted error code. 3. Determine whether the failure is deterministic data validation, transient infrastructure, adapter incompatibility, or a domain invariant failure. 4. For transient failures, restore the dependency and resume from the recorded checkpoint. Idempotency and external reference uniqueness must make replay safe. 5. For bad inputs or mappings, cancel the job, create immutable corrected inputs/configuration, and run a new dry run. Do not mutate committed evidence. 6. Reconcile row counts, external references, entity totals, currencies, historical payment/refund snapshots, ticket state, and check in history before activation. 7. If partial writes cannot be proven safe, keep the job paused, disable activation, and escalate with the corrective plan. Do not force completion. Alert on stalled progress, repeated chunk failures, conflict spikes, tenant scope violations, input hash mismatches, reconciliation drift, rollback refusal, and accidental side effect attempts. Operational dashboards and audit logs must use job/entity identifiers and error codes rather than buyer PII. Release and compatibility Pin the migration adapter and source version matrix used by every job. Adapter upgrades do not alter an existing job’s semantics. Breaking mapping or normalization changes require a new adapter major version, migration guide, fixtures, dry run/commit/idempotency tests, and an explicit operator choice for new jobs.

title: Build a bespoke migration adapter
description: Author and validate an organization-specific adapter without scraping.
body: Use defineBespokeAdapter and runBespokeAdapterConformance from @tixkit/migration core . Adapters must use official APIs or customer provided exports, declare supported versions, feature mappings, known losses, rate limit behavior, and implement deterministic discover, extract, normalize, and validate operations. Never place source credentials in configuration, fixtures, normalized rows, or logs. Resolve scoped references only in non replayable worker activities. External IDs must be stable; dependencies must follow the platform order; financial history must use side effect suppressed snapshots. Before registration, provide sanitized fixtures and prove dry run determinism, bounded cursors, validation severities, re import idempotency, historical financial semantics, and rollback eligibility. The executable conformance runner is offline and does not permit scraping or hidden network behavior. See the package authoring README for the complete contract.

title: Migrate from Eventbrite
description: Import Eventbrite API v3 or official attendee exports.
body: Supported sources are Eventbrite API v3 and official attendee CSV exports dated 2024 01 through 2026 07. Events, ticket classes, attendees, historical orders, tickets, discounts, check ins, and historical payment/refund snapshots are mapped with stable Eventbrite IDs. Organizer payout schedules remain source provenance only. Reserved seating geometry and marketing audiences are known losses. Imported financial history cannot create provider success events. Use continuation tokens, pages of at most 100 records, Retry After , and bounded exponential backoff. Keep the official export immutable, run dry run and known loss review, then commit. Re import and pre activation rollback eligibility are covered by the adapter conformance profile. In the migration workspace, choose Official API , enter the Eventbrite organization ID, and select at least one explicit event ID. Event IDs are required so the bounded resource plan is durable and resumable; organization wide event discovery is not performed implicitly. The resulting non secret configuration is exactly: Select the expiring credential reference separately; tokens and cursor URLs are not configuration fields.

title: Import Generic CSV exports
description: Prepare, map, preview, and migrate deterministic CSV exports.
body: The Generic CSV adapter accepts immutable RFC 4180 documents for events, ticket types, attendees, historical orders, tickets, promo codes, and check in history. Use rfc4180 v1 ; template files and sample data are exported by @tixkit/migration core . The adapter detects comma, semicolon, tab, or pipe delimiters and recognizes entity headers. Always confirm detection in the preview, save an organization scoped mapping profile, and rerun dry run after any mapping change. Required source IDs become stable external references, so re importing an unchanged export skips existing records. Supported mappings include fixed ticket prices and capacity, attendee/buyer provenance, historical orders, issued tickets, fixed or percentage promo codes, and check in/check out timestamps. Reserved seat geometry, provider payment success, source messaging, and webhook automation are reported as known losses. Historical order status never creates a successful provider payment. Import spreadsheet formulas only as data. Error CSV output prefixes formula leading values and can be safely opened for remediation. Resolve every fatal/error row, verify timezone and ISO currency findings, then commit with the job bound confirmation. Rollback remains limited to untouched entities created by that job.

title: Migrate from Hi.Events
description: Import supported Hi.Events API or export bundles.
body: Supported sources are REST API v1 for Hi.Events 0.20–0.x and official JSON/CSV export bundles. The adapter covers organizations/brands, venues, events/occurrences, capacity assignments, products/ticket types, questions, promo/access codes, buyers/attendees, historical orders, tickets, historical payments/refunds, and check ins. Organizer dashboard widgets are not portable. Provider specific payment metadata is retained only as sanitized snapshot provenance. Financial snapshots never trigger live payment or fulfillment behavior. Collection honors official Retry After guidance and bounded retries for 429/502/503/504. Pin the adapter version, preserve the source page cursors, run dry run, review losses and counts, and commit only the hash current job. Stable source IDs make retries and re import idempotent. In the migration workspace, choose Official API and enter the account ID, one or more event IDs, and—only for self hosting—the HTTPS API origin. The resulting non secret configuration is exactly: Select an expiring credential reference separately. Never paste an API key, cursor, response record, or arbitrary URL into the scope fields.

title: Migrate from pretix
description: Import supported pretix REST API or official export data.
body: Supported sources are pretix REST API v1 for pretix 2023.7–2026.x and Organizer Data Shredder compatible JSON exports. Use official API/export data only. The adapter maps organizers/brands, venues, events/occurrences, quotas, items/products, questions, vouchers, buyers/attendees, historical orders, tickets, historical payment/refund snapshots, and check ins in dependency order. Assigned seat geometry is reported but not imported. Plugin fields without scalar export values require a bespoke mapper. Payment and refund records retain amount, currency, provider reference, timestamp, and provenance but never emit provider success, fulfillment, notification, or webhook side effects. API collection honors Retry After , uses official cursors, and retries 429/502/503/504 with deterministic bounded exponential delay. Store only the scoped secret manager reference. Dry run the complete immutable page/export set, review known losses, then commit. Re import uses pretix IDs as stable external references; rollback tests must remain green before activation. In the migration workspace, choose Official API and enter the organizer slug, one or more event slugs, and—only for self hosted pretix—the HTTPS API origin. The resulting non secret configuration is exactly: Credentials are selected separately by credential reference. Do not put tokens, cursor URLs, query strings, or response records in configuration.

title: Migrate from Ticket Tailor
description: Import Ticket Tailor API v1 or official order exports.
body: Supported sources are Ticket Tailor API v1 and official Orders exports dated 2024 01 through 2026 07. The adapter maps events, ticket types, historical orders, issued tickets, vouchers, check ins, and side effect suppressed payment/refund snapshots. Waitlist notification history and broadcast audiences are not imported. Checkout layout is flattened into question records. Historical payments and refunds remain immutable snapshots. Follow official next link cursors, cap pages at 100, honor Retry After , and use bounded retries for 429/5xx. Preserve source IDs and exports, approve dry run losses/counts, and activate only after reconciliation. Unchanged re imports skip existing references. In the migration workspace, choose Official API and enter the account ID plus one or more event IDs. The resulting non secret configuration is exactly: Ticket Tailor credentials are selected separately by credential reference. Do not place Basic auth material, continuation URLs, or response data in job configuration.

title: Find and understand orders
description: Inspect order, payment, fulfillment, and compensation state without exposing buyer data.
body: Use the Orders area to find a purchase and understand its current state. Treat order status, payment provider status, workflow state, and attendee fulfillment as related but distinct evidence. Find the order Search with the least sensitive identifier available, such as an order reference supplied through an authorized support channel. Confirm the organization, brand, event, amount, currency, creation time, and line items before taking action. Do not paste full buyer records, payment details, or ticket codes into chat, issue trackers, or screenshots. Interpret state A successful payment does not automatically prove every downstream activity completed. Review the order timeline and compensation indicators for pending or failed workflows. If the provider and Tixkit disagree, preserve non secret correlation identifiers and follow the payment reconciliation runbook. Retry safely Use only explicit retry or repair actions offered by the dashboard. Refreshing a page is safe; resubmitting a checkout or manually changing database state is not a repair. If an action is disabled, resolve the shown permission or state prerequisite. Continue with refunds /operators/orders/refunds or attendee records /operators/attendees .

title: Process and diagnose refunds
description: Validate eligibility, initiate a refund once, and confirm provider and order compensation state.
body: Refunds can have external financial side effects. Confirm environment, order, amount, currency, and provider mode before submitting. Validate eligibility Open the order detail view and review prior refunds, payment status, remaining refundable amount, and any compensation warning. In capture mode, behavior is local. In provider test or production mode, the refund may call the configured provider. Submit once Enter the authorized amount and reason, review the confirmation, and submit once. Wait for the resulting state instead of repeating the action. Tixkit uses idempotent/durable processing, but repeated operator requests make incident diagnosis harder. Verify completion Confirm the refund record and order totals after the workflow settles. Where provider access is available, reconcile the provider reference without copying credentials or customer payment data. If state remains pending or failed, use the dashboard's compensation details and incident runbooks /operations/incidents . Do not mark an order refunded solely because a toast or provider page appeared.

title: Run reports and exports
description: Request scoped reporting data, monitor asynchronous exports, and handle generated files safely.
