body: Reports and exports inherit the active tenant, organization, brand, event, and permission context. Treat generated files as potentially sensitive operational data. Run a report Confirm the selected context and time range before applying filters. Validate totals against a small known sample when the report informs financial or attendance decisions. Create an export Submit the export once and monitor its job state. Exports may be produced asynchronously by workflow activities and object storage. A request acknowledgement is not proof the file exists. Download only through the authorized link, store the file according to your retention policy, and do not attach customer data to public issues. Diagnose failure Check the job event/status shown by the dashboard. Distinguish query validation, workflow/worker, object storage, and signed download failures. Use incident runbooks /operations/incidents for a stuck job rather than recreating many identical exports.

title: Operate the integration sandbox
description: Initialize, reset, isolate, and recover Tixkit's deterministic integration sandbox.
body: The sandbox must use a dedicated database, object storage namespace, and Temporal task queue. Set TIXKIT RUNTIME MODE=sandbox ; this forces payment, refund, email, and SMS activities onto capture/no provider behavior even if provider credentials are accidentally present. Initialize a new migrated sandbox database once with TIXKIT SANDBOX INITIALIZE CONFIRM="INITIALIZE " and tixkit sandbox:initialize . The marker is persisted inside the target database. Reset refuses an unmarked database, a primary database alias, a database outside the anchored tixkit sandbox / tixkit test naming convention, or remote reset without the explicit remote reset flag. Stop and drain every sandbox API and worker process, then set TIXKIT SANDBOX RESET COORDINATION=STOPPED only for tixkit sandbox:reset . The result shows a scoped 24 hour API key once and returns epoch plus taskQueue . Configure both API and worker with TIXKIT SANDBOX EPOCH= and TEMPORAL TASK QUEUE= . Startup compares these values with the persisted database marker and fails closed for stale epochs or another queue. Scheduler workflow IDs are epoch scoped, so the new worker cannot reuse a scheduler bound to the prior queue. Each reset seeds the canonical sample brand/event, a future event window, free and capture paid admission, a hidden access code ticket SANDBOX VIP , promotion, add on, checkout question, check in list, and sample history. Old credentials disappear with the reset; old task queues have no worker in the new epoch. If sandbox traffic reaches a provider, stop API/workers, revoke the exposed provider credential, preserve non payload correlation IDs, initialize/reset the sandbox, rotate the task queue, and verify sandbox runtime mode before restoring access.

title: Manage team access and permissions
description: Grant the minimum dashboard capabilities required for each operating role.
body: Dashboard permissions govern actions such as event, ticket, order, refund, attendee, check in, box office, messaging, report, settings, developer, and billing work. Grant only the capabilities required for the person's role. Review before granting Confirm the intended tenant and organization, the user's identity, and their operational responsibility. Separate door/check in work from settings, developer credentials, refunds, and billing unless the role genuinely requires both. Verify the result After saving access, ask the teammate to reload their authenticated session. They should see permitted navigation and receive a clear blocked state for unauthorized actions. Hidden navigation alone is not authorization; the API must enforce the same boundary. Remove access promptly Remove or reduce access when a responsibility changes. Rotate any separately issued API key or device credential; changing a dashboard role does not revoke credentials owned by another authentication system. Report any cross tenant or permission bypass through the private security process /support , without including customer data or secrets.

title: Configure workspace and organization context
description: Select the correct tenant organization and brand before making scoped operational changes.
body: Tixkit scopes operational data by tenant, organization, and brand. Always confirm the active context before creating an event, connecting a provider, or inviting a teammate. Confirm the selected context Use the organization and brand selectors in the authenticated dashboard shell. After changing context, wait for the scoped bootstrap data to reload. The event, payment, developer, and reporting views must reflect the new selection before you continue. Update workspace identity Open Settings → Workspace . Review the display identity and any organization settings available to your permission set. Save once, then reload the page to verify the API persisted the value. Users without settings permission may read permitted workspace context but must not be shown a change action. Ask a workspace owner to make the change rather than sharing credentials. Diagnose a context mismatch If expected events or orders disappear, recheck the selected organization and brand. If an action returns forbidden, confirm both the active context and your permission. If the selector offers an unexpected tenant, stop and report the isolation issue without copying customer data into the report. Continue with brand configuration /operators/brands or team access /operators/team and permissions .

title: Connect an agent through the Platform API
description: Register explicit agent identities and grant bounded, sponsor-controlled authority.

headings.text: Read aggregate event sales without approval
Prepare an event update without approval
Prepare and execute an event update
Persist and inspect an approval-aware plan
Prove an orchestrator against the shared contract

body: Experimental private beta: the shared identity and delegation contract is public for evaluation. Hosted agent access, managed models, natural language orchestration, managed prompts, evaluations and managed memory are not generally available. Use only an invited environment and its supplied support channel. Tixkit agents use explicit principals. An agent does not impersonate its organizer sponsor and cannot write directly to a database. Authorization is evaluated through the existing API and workflow boundaries. Current beta surface API version 2026 08 08 , action protocol 2026 07 22 , plan protocol 2026 07 27 and action registry contract 2026 08 04 support these sponsor controlled operations: register an agent principal; read a principal sponsored by the current user; revoke a principal and its active delegations atomically; grant and revoke time bounded event delegations; create, inspect, correct, export and delete separately retained organizer memory; create and revoke sponsor bound OAuth clients for active agents; exchange client credentials and inspect an explicit, permission empty agent session; read a bounded, version bound event projection with explicit untrusted content provenance; read an aggregate only event sales report for an exact closed time range; prepare a normalized, version bound event update preview without mutating event or media state; canonicalize and preview a safe event page document without mutating product state; prepare exact published campaign content, audience, consent and suppression evidence without queueing delivery; prepare, freshly approve, execute and exactly replay a normalized, version bound event update; read event readiness through a direct, immutable, digest bound action result; prepare and retrieve an immutable event.publish action with a server authoritative dry run; persist, inspect and version an immutable multi step plan over prepared actions; issue a short lived, digest bound human approval; revoke an unconsumed approval through an action bound, digest bound lifecycle event; and execute approved event.publish and event.update actions through durable, idempotent typed operations. The initial capabilities are events.read , reports.read , readiness.read , events.prepare , content.prepare , campaigns.prepare and events.execute . Consequential execution still requires a typed action and fresh approval; plan supported actions additionally bind approval to an immutable plan digest. The registration API does not grant unrestricted delegated autonomy, campaign sending or buyer purchasing. Authenticate the sponsor Agent administration accepts only a human bearer principal with tenant wide developers.write . API keys, mobile principals, system principals and users restricted to selected brands or events fail closed. The sponsor must also hold the current event permission implied by every requested capability. Do not give the agent the sponsor's session. Register the agent while acting as the human sponsor, then use the returned principal identifier in later delegation requests. Authenticate the agent Create a credential with POST /v1/agent principals/{id}/oauth clients . Its organization is credential administration ownership only; it does not grant event access. Store the returned clientSecret immediately because it is shown once and omitted from idempotent replays. Multiple clients are supported so you can create a replacement before revoking the old credential. Exchange the client ID and secret at POST /v1/oauth/token with grant type=client credentials . Use HTTP Basic or JSON/form fields, never both and never query parameters. The response is a ten minute tk aat ... token with fixed agent.invoke scope and no refresh token. The JavaScript SDK exposes this server side flow as tixkit.agentAuth.exchangeClientCredentials . Call GET /v1/agent/session with that token to verify the live explicit principal. The session has no organization authority or product permissions. Agent authentication never copies sponsor scopes: current delegation and policy checks remain separate and mandatory for every action. All generic authenticated routes deny agent principals unless their route contract explicitly opts in. Client or principal revocation takes effect on the next request. Register an explicit principal Send a stable caller reference, the agent kind, requested capabilities and maximum autonomy to POST /v1/agent principals . Every mutation requires a unique Idempotency Key of 16–255 characters. The server derives the tenant, sponsor, protocol version, active state, registration time and tenant namespaced identifier. Managed Cloud currently accepts third party ; Self Hosted may additionally enable self hosted for a bring your own orchestrator. Store the returned agt ... identifier. Reusing an idempotency key with different intent returns a conflict. Grant bounded authority Send the returned principal identifier, capabilities, explicit event: scopes and a future expiry to POST /v1/agent delegations . A grant may cover at most 100 unique event scopes and 30 days. Inside the transaction, Tixkit rechecks the sponsor's current permission grants, accepted organization membership, event ownership and active principal state. The service derives issuedAt and permissionSnapshot ; clients cannot submit either field. A material authorization change requires a new grant or approval. Revoke and inspect The sponsor can inspect only their own principal and can revoke their own principals or delegations. Cross sponsor resources are returned as not found. Principal revocation cascades to active delegations. Every mutation is idempotent, audited and reauthorizes the human actor before replay. Read event configuration without approval An explicitly authenticated agent calls tixkit.agentActions.readEvent or POST /v1/agent/events with an event identifier, matching delegation grant and idempotency key. The server requires events.read in the principal and delegation, exact event: scope, current sponsor events.read authority and accepted organization membership, plus an allowing event.read action/risk policy. The terminal result is a strict subset of the versioned event: title, description, lifecycle status, currency, timezone, schedule, visibility, capacity and minimum age. It excludes credentials, provider state, buyer/payment data, arbitrary metadata and SEO configuration. eventSnapshotSha256 binds the projection to the immutable action; resultSha256 binds the complete timestamped result. untrustedContentPaths is exactly 'event.title', 'event.description' , identifying organizer authored strings that an orchestrator must treat as data rather than instructions. Exact replay and GET /v1/agent/events/{actionId} recheck the complete current authorization intersection. Revocation, permission or membership loss, scope or policy denial, and resource or policy version drift fail closed. event.read cannot enter a plan and cannot create approval, execution or product effects. Read aggregate event sales without approval An explicitly authenticated agent calls tixkit.agentActions.readReport or POST /v1/agent/reports with an event identifier, matching delegation, idempotency key, and either both canonical UTC whole second bounds or neither. The server requires reports.read in the principal and delegation, exact event: scope, a reports:read delegation snapshot, current sponsor reports.read authority and accepted membership, plus allowing report.read action and risk policies. The terminal result contains only currency, sales and channel totals, net revenue, refunds, fees, tax, tickets sold, check ins and order counts for the exact closed range. It excludes orders, buyers, attendees, contact data and payment details. When bounds are omitted, the server derives them from event creation through the database observation time. reportSnapshotSha256 binds the coherent aggregate projection; the action digest binds that snapshot to the event version and normalized range, and resultSha256 binds the complete timestamped result. Exact replay and GET /v1/agent/reports/{actionId} reauthorize and recompute that same range. Revocation, expiry, permission or membership loss, scope or policy denial, event version drift, relevant in range data drift and persisted evidence substitution fail closed; changes outside the range do not invalidate it. report.read is direct only and cannot enter a plan or create approval, execution, export or product effects. Prepare an event update without approval An explicitly authenticated agent calls tixkit.agentActions.prepareEvent or POST /v1/agent/event preparations with an event identifier, matching delegation, idempotency key and non empty changes . The accepted change object is the complete generic event PATCH surface except status and expectedVersion ; lifecycle status remains confined to its dedicated operations. The server requires events.prepare in the principal and delegation, exact event scope, current sponsor events.write authority and membership, plus an allowing event.prepare action/risk policy. Resolution uses the same slug, venue, media ownership and normalization rules as organizer PATCH. It validates owned, clean media without renewing its lease and performs no event, venue, upload, approval, execution or plan write. The action payload binds the canonical normalized changes and changePreviewSha256 ; the result binds the exact resource version, sorted material fields, before/after projections, observation time and result digest. Every before. and after. path is declared untrusted because existing and proposed organizer controlled content is data, never an instruction. Derived organizer visible effects, such as the venue snapshot resolved from venueId , are included in the field set and digest even when the request supplies only the identifier. Exact replay and GET /v1/agent/event preparations/{actionId} reauthorize the full intersection and return identical persisted evidence. Event or policy version drift, revocation, permission or membership loss, scope denial, slug conflict, foreign venue, foreign or unsafe media, malformed input and persisted evidence substitution fail closed. event.prepare is direct only and cannot be approved or executed. Prepare event page content without approval An explicitly authenticated agent calls tixkit.agentActions.prepareContent or POST /v1/agent/content preparations with exactly a delegation identifier, event identifier and event page document. The server requires the content.prepare capability, exact event scope, a delegation snapshot and current sponsor authority containing events:write , accepted membership, and allowing action/risk policies. It locks and versions the event before deriving any organizer visible context. The adapter accepts only channel event page and the safe initial Puck subset: EventHeader , EventDescription , Divider , Tickets , ResaleTickets , CheckoutCta and BrandFooter . Input is bounded by canonical bytes, depth, collection size and string size. Unknown fields are stripped against server owned templates; unsupported components, CustomEmbed , populated zones, cyclic values, non finite numbers and oversized input fail closed. The original is never treated as an instruction. Discovery fields are derived from the same locked event snapshot, validation exposes bounded reason codes rather than raw parser text, and content plus preview.discovery are explicitly declared untrusted. The result binds canonical content, derived preview, validation, event version and contentPreviewSha256 into immutable action and result digests. Exact replay and GET /v1/agent/content preparations/{actionId} reauthorize capability, delegation, sponsor permission, policy and event version before returning identical persisted evidence. The operation writes only action, result and audit evidence: it does not update the event page, uploads, products or other organizer state, cannot enter a plan, and cannot be approved or executed. Prepare a campaign without sending An explicitly authenticated agent calls tixkit.agentActions.prepareCampaign or POST /v1/agent/campaign preparations with a delegation, event, audience, channel and the required published template keys. The server requires campaigns.prepare , exact event scope, a messages:write delegation snapshot, current sponsor messages.write , accepted membership and allowing action/risk policies. specific audiences accept 1–1,000 unique attendee identifiers; all other audiences reject attendee identifiers. Channel and template fields must match exactly. The adapter locks the event and resolves the same audience, consent, suppression and published content decisions used by organizer campaign delivery. Consent must match the attendee's current normalized contact, email suppression lookup is case and whitespace insensitive, and the response contains aggregate counts and version identifiers without contact data. Separate digests bind exact content versions, matched audience, exclusions and compliance evidence, including non PII consent and suppression record provenance. Exact replay and GET /v1/agent/campaign preparations/{actionId} reauthorize and recompute every snapshot; content, audience, contact, consent, suppression, event, policy or authority drift fails closed. Preparation creates only action, result and audit evidence. It creates no email or SMS jobs, cannot enter a plan, and exposes no approval or execution route. Campaign sending remains outside this release and requires a separate consequential action with exact content/audience approval and fresh consent/suppression evaluation. Prepare and execute an event update An explicitly authenticated agent calls tixkit.agentActions.prepareEventUpdate or POST /v1/agent/event updates with the same bounded non status patch surface. The server requires events.execute , exact event scope, an events:write delegation snapshot, current sponsor events.write , accepted membership and allowing event.update policies. It resolves the exact normalized preview without mutation and persists preview , previewSha256 , action digest, authorization evidence and expiry. Exact preparation replay returns identical evidence; GET /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId} supports later inspection. The human sponsor reviews the complete before/after projection and calls tixkit.agentActions.approveEventUpdate or POST /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId}/approvals with confirmation approve: : . The explicit agent calls tixkit.agentActions.executeEventUpdate or POST /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId}/executions with both idempotency and confirmation set to execute: : : . Revocation and evidence retrieval remain on the same dedicated event updates surface. Inside a serializable transaction, Tixkit locks the authoritative state, rechecks the principal, delegation, sponsor, permission, policy, approval, execution fence and resource version, then re resolves slug, venue and owned media state from the persisted changes. Any no op or preview drift invalidates the approval. One successful transaction applies the optimistic event update and atomically records agent attributed product audit plus durable effect evidence. The only public result is the event identifier, exactly one incremented resource version and status updated . Exact retries converge on that evidence, including recovery after a committed effect. Automatic compensation is unavailable: an inverse change is a new version bound action requiring fresh approval. event.update remains direct only in 2026 08 04 ; it cannot be inserted into a plan. Read event readiness without approval An explicitly authenticated agent calls tixkit.agentActions.readReadiness or POST /v1/agent/readiness with an event identifier, a matching delegation grant and an idempotency key. The server requires readiness.read in the principal capability and delegation, exact event: scope, live sponsor events.read authority, an events:read permission snapshot, and an allowed current tenant action and risk policy. The response is terminal: it contains an immutable action, action digest, authorization and dry run evidence, plus a canonical result and resultSha256 . The result reports the current event version, readiness status and snapshot digest, publication state, blocker and warning reason codes, and a server derived timestamp. Exact replay returns the identical persisted evidence only while the complete current authorization intersection still passes. Principal or delegation revocation, sponsor permission or membership loss, scope or policy denial, and resource or policy version changes deny both replay and GET /v1/agent/readiness/{actionId} . The operation never mutates product state, never accepts approval, never creates an execution record and cannot be placed in a plan. Approval or execution attempts against it fail closed. Use a new idempotency key to observe a later state. A changed event or policy cannot be hidden behind a reused key, and a key reused for different intent returns a conflict. Prepare and execute event publication An explicitly authenticated agent prepares an event publish action through tixkit.agentActions.prepare or POST /v1/agent/actions . The request contains only the action kind, delegation identifier and event identifier. The server derives identity, sponsor, tenant, resource and policy versions, exact readiness digest, operation and preparation time under a serializable transaction. The resulting action and dry run evidence are immutable, expire after at most 15 minutes and converge on exact idempotent replay. Cross agent reads fail closed. Preparation never authorizes execution. eligibleForApproval means only that the live authorization intersection and event readiness passed except for the mandatory approval. A human sponsor with current events.write permission issues approval through tixkit.agentActions.approve or POST /v1/agent/actions/{actionId}/approvals . A standalone request carries the exact action digest and confirmation approve: : . Once an action belongs to an authoritative plan, planSha256 is mandatory and confirmation must be approve: : : . Tixkit revalidates the exact plan, step, completed dependencies, principal, delegation, sponsor, tenant membership, permission, policy, risk, resource version and readiness digest inside the serializable transaction. The resulting approval expires after at most five minutes or at plan expiry, whichever occurs first, and cannot be reused for another action or plan. An exact replay returns the original approval even if authority has since changed, without creating new authority. A new approval request after any material readiness, policy, resource, delegation or permission change fails closed. The exact human sponsor revokes an unconsumed approval through tixkit.agentActions.revokeApproval or POST /v1/agent/actions/{actionId}/approvals/{approvalId}/revoke . Revocation remains available after event permission loss, requires the exact action digest and explicit confirmation, converges under exact replay and records one immutable lifecycle event. Cross sponsor, cross tenant, changed binding and consumed approval attempts fail closed. The exact authenticated agent executes through tixkit.agentActions.execute or POST /v1/agent/actions/{actionId}/executions . Send only the approval identifier and exact action digest, with both Idempotency Key and X Tixkit Confirmation equal to execute: : : . Tixkit atomically consumes the unrevoked approval and reserves durable execution evidence. Planned execution is persisted with the plan digest. The typed event publish boundary locks and rechecks the current plan and step alongside the principal, delegation, sponsor membership and permission, tenant and risk policy, event version, approval binding and readiness digest before changing the event. Cancellation wins before reservation or effect application; once an execution exists, cancellation is rejected rather than claiming that a consequential effect was stopped. One execution can create at most one recorded product effect. An exact retry after a terminal result returns the same evidence. A retry while another worker holds the execution lease may return 409 ; retry it without changing the action, approval or digest. Permanent authorization changes are recorded as a bounded failed execution, while retryable infrastructure faults leave the leased execution resumable. Approval consumption is consequential: a consumed approval cannot be revoked or transferred to another execution. The exact agent or human sponsor inspects durable execution and its ordered immutable audit history through tixkit.agentActions.getExecution or GET /v1/agent/actions/{actionId}/executions/{executionId} . Sponsor access remains available after event permission loss for accountability. Cross tenant, cross principal, cross sponsor and cross action lookups return not found; corrupt or incomplete audit evidence fails closed. Persist and inspect an approval aware plan After preparing every plan supported typed action, the authenticated agent submits the canonical 2026 07 27 plan definition and exact step to action bindings through tixkit.agentPlans.create or POST /v1/agent/plans . The database reloads those actions and rechecks the agent, sponsor, delegation, capabilities, resource scopes, action digests and lifetime. Creation has no product effect and grants no approval. The 2026 08 04 registry marks event.read , report.read , readiness.read , event.prepare , content.prepare , campaign.prepare and event.update as direct only, so they are evidence or standalone approved actions rather than plan steps. The exact agent or sponsor reads the immutable definition, bindings and current state through tixkit.agentPlans.get or GET /v1/agent/plans/{planId} . Advance state with tixkit.agentPlans.transition or POST /v1/agent/plans/{planId}/transitions . Supply an expected state version, complete next step states, a bounded reason code and an idempotency key. Tixkit owns timestamps and reloads approvals and executions under lock; clients cannot assert their own evidence. Dependencies, fresh approvals, approval consumption, execution bindings and terminal result digests are validated before the compare and swap update. Each accepted transition appends immutable before and after state plus canonical, digest bound actor authorization evidence. Cross tenant identifiers remain isolated and material authorization changes fail closed. Memory and managed tools Agent memory is separately retained, scoped, inspectable, correctable, exportable and deletable. Human sponsors manage it through tixkit.agentMemory or the /v1/agent memory operations. Namespace ownership and organizer provenance are server derived. Reads and exports are audited, corrections and deletions are version aware, and each export contains a checksum over that exact timestamped bundle. Deletion removes content while retaining digest only audit evidence. The durable maintenance workflow physically erases expired content in bounded, retryable batches. Workspace and event scopes recheck current database authorization; project scope remains unavailable until a durable project resource exists. Memory content accepts only the typed organizer preferences and project context shapes. Credentials, payment data, buyer data and personal contact data fail closed. Agent retrieval remains delegation bound through the shared repository and is not a generic HTTP read capability. Campaign preparation is an agent tool with exact consent, suppression, content and audience evidence but no sending authority. A future managed sending tool additionally requires exact content and audience approval plus fresh consent and suppression evaluation. Natural language orchestration and managed memory remain Cloud capabilities; self hosters may bring an orchestrator through the shared protocol. Prove an orchestrator against the shared contract The public @tixkit/contract tests source package includes a live agent platform profile for third party and Self Hosted orchestrators. It verifies direct event and aggregate report reads, event preparation, safe content preparation and consent/suppression aware campaign preparation, rejection of approval/execution for direct only actions, an approval bound event update with exact execution replay, readiness evidence and the plan bound event.publish golden path: client credential authentication, explicit agent identity, version/digest and untrusted content binding, typed action preparation, fresh sponsor approval, idempotent execution, canonical plan persistence, terminal plan state and audit evidence against one API environment. It does not claim hosted availability or cover the separate memory and revocation contracts. This profile reads a bounded aggregate sales report, prepares event page content and a campaign, changes the event title and description, then publishes it. Use only an isolated private beta or Self Hosted test tenant and an unpublished disposable event that is ready to publish. The fixture's campaign template must already be published and its audience must contain eligible consented recipients; the profile proves no message jobs are sent only through returned contract evidence, so run it in an environment whose provider routes are isolated. Never run it against a production event. The sponsor must own the agent and retain events.read , reports.read , events.write and messages.write ; the agent delegation must grant events.read , reports.read , readiness.read , events.prepare , content.prepare , campaigns.prepare and events.execute for that exact event. Install the runner and create a fixture containing identifiers and environment variable names, never credential values: The command exits nonzero and emits structured, credential free findings if any identity, cache control, protocol, digest, state or audit invariant fails. Use a new plan ID and idempotency prefix for each disposable event.

title: Add ticketing to my product
description: Integrate ticketing through the Tixkit Platform API, SDKs, webhooks, and embeds.
body: The Tixkit Platform API is the developer facing capability inside Tixkit Cloud. It shares the same event, inventory, checkout, order, attendee, webhook, workflow, migration, OpenAPI, and SDK contracts as the rest of Tixkit. Availability: hosted Platform API access is planned for an experimental private beta. Public API contracts and SDK source are available for evaluation, but production Cloud credentials and support terms are not generally available. Make a safe first integration 1. Follow the hosted Platform API quickstart /platform/quickstart if you have a private beta invitation, or read it to understand the intended credential and environment flow. 2. Read the API fundamentals /developers/api fundamentals , including tenant scope, authentication, permissions, idempotency, pagination, errors, and retries. 3. Make the first API call /getting started/first api call with the narrowest useful credential scope. 4. Choose a supported SDK /sdks/javascript or use the generated OpenAPI contract directly. 5. Configure webhooks /developers/webhooks/setup , verify every signature, and make consumers idempotent. 6. Add the embedded widget /developers/widget/embedding only after the server side contract and failure behavior are understood. Agent connections Third party agents connect through the same Platform API. API version 2026 08 08 exposes experimental sponsor bound principals, delegation, short lived explicit agent authentication, an isolated session surface, direct version bound event.read projections, aggregate only report.read evidence, direct mutation free event.prepare previews, bounded safe content.prepare event page previews, consent/suppression aware and send free campaign.prepare evidence, freshly approved and version safe event.update execution, digest bound readiness.read evidence, server derived event.publish action preparation, immutable approval aware plans, short lived digest bound human approval, action bound revocation and durable approved execution. Untrusted organizer content is explicitly declared and never interpreted as tool instruction. A public live conformance profile validates direct event and report reads, preparation approval/execution rejection, approved update replay and the plan bound event.publish golden path in invited and Self Hosted test environments. Current repository evidence covers fresh local PostgreSQL and MySQL integration, mocked transport and packed fail closed execution; no hosted environment has been certified. Read the agent Platform API guide /platform/agent platform for the implemented boundary, runner and current private beta limitations. Continue Make the first API call /getting started/first api call , browse the API reference /reference/api , or choose an SDK guide /sdks/javascript .

title: Start with the hosted Platform API
description: Use an invited Cloud environment and scoped credential for a safe first API request.
body: Experimental private beta: hosted Platform API access is not generally available. Use only the environment identifier, API origin, credential flow, and support channel supplied in an invitation. Public examples do not grant access. Confirm the invited environment Sign in through the invitation and verify the expected organization, environment, region, and permissions. Keep sandbox and production credentials separate. If any identifier differs from the invitation, stop before creating a key. Create a read only credential Create a server side credential with the narrowest scope needed to list events. Copy its secret once into a secret manager or an ephemeral shell. Never place it in browser code, URLs, screenshots, analytics, support messages, or client visible environment variables. Set the exact origin from the invitation; this guide intentionally provides no default hosted origin: Paste the secret only at the silent prompt, then run unset TIXKIT API KEY when the session ends. The secret must never appear in shell history, command arguments, or a committed environment file. Make a read only request config reads the expanded header from standard input, so the secret is not placed in curl's process arguments or a temporary file. An empty event list is valid. Treat 401 as a credential problem, 403 as a permission or tenant scope denial, 404 as an environment or path mismatch, and 429 as a signal to honor the supplied retry policy. Do not broaden scopes to bypass a denial. Add webhook verification Create a test endpoint, store its signing secret separately from the API key, verify signatures before parsing /developers/webhooks/verify signatures , reject stale timestamps, and make processing idempotent. Revoke the credential immediately if it appeared in client code or logs. Continue Review API fundamentals /developers/api fundamentals , the generated reference /reference/api , and the SDK guides /sdks/javascript . Invited agent integrators should also read the agent Platform API guide /platform/agent platform . The shared principal, delegation, typed action, approval, execution, audit, memory and live conformance contracts are public; hosted exposure remains invitation limited and is not generally available.

title: Accessibility conformance
description: Understand the accessibility target, tested documentation and product surfaces, and known reporting path.
body: Tixkit targets keyboard operable, screen reader compatible, responsive interfaces with visible focus, semantic landmarks/headings, appropriate contrast, reduced motion behavior, and accessible error/status communication. Documentation acceptance covers homepage, representative guide, search, API reference, mobile navigation, code copy, and framework tabs across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with axe, console, and page error gates. Product conformance remains limited to the surfaces and evidence named by the repository validation record; this page does not claim certification. Report an accessibility problem through support /support with route, browser/assistive technology, steps, expected behavior, and a data safe description.

title: API contract release train
description: Versioning, compatibility, verification, and publication gates for Tixkit API and SDK contracts.
body: API contract release train Every contract release is stored under artifacts/api/ and exposed by the documentation site at /contracts/ / . A release contains OpenAPI JSON and YAML, generated TypeScript declarations, the webhook catalog, sanitized examples, an API diff, a changelog, a manifest, and SHA 256 checksums. The API version uses a date. Additive operations and optional fields may ship within the current version. Removing an operation or named schema is detected as breaking and fails the release build. A breaking contract requires a new API version, migration guidance, SDK compatibility updates, and explicit release approval. The current and immediately previous versions remain supported during the documented deprecation window. Before release, run: The API Contract Release workflow repeats these gates and uploads a private workflow artifact. It does not publish a package, create a public release, upload production CDN content, or create a tag. Those actions require the protected api contract production environment and final release approval. After approved publication, verify each registry or CDN object by downloading it into a clean directory, comparing its SHA 256 value with CHECKSUMS.sha256 , installing the packed SDK, running the SDK consumer contract, and confirming that the public release manifest source commit is an ancestor of the approved tag commit. Incident and rollback procedure If any checksum, attestation, manifest commit, registry package, documentation copy, or staged CDN object disagrees, stop before advancing an alias or tag and retain every candidate plus workflow log as incident evidence. Never overwrite an immutable version. For a partial publication, restore the prior documentation/CDN alias atomically, purge only mutable caches, and verify the previous manifest again. Deprecate a bad registry package with a corrective message instead of deleting or republishing its version. Retract any pending deprecation window, publish a corrective compatibility plan, and notify affected consumers only through the approved incident channel. Production aliases, package publication, tags, and consumer communication remain external approval actions.

title: Migrate from API 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-12
description: Replace legacy event upload URLs with role-based public media renditions.
body: Migrate from API 2026 01 01 to 2026 07 12 The 2026 07 12 contract removes GET /public/event media/{purpose}/{artifactId} . That legacy route addressed an upload artifact directly and could not express publication state, media role, or a sanitized rendition. It is not available in the new version. Read public event media from PublicEvent.mediaAssets . Select a role poster , cover , or social and a rendition thumbnail , page , or social , then use that rendition's url . Rendition URLs are publication aware and serve normalized, metadata stripped WebP content. For organizer applications, upload the original through the upload artifact flow and attach it with PUT /events/{eventId}/media/{role} . Do not persist upload download URLs as buyer facing media. Clients that do not use event media require no changes. mediaAssets is optional in the schema so clients can continue to read events produced by older deployments during a rolling upgrade.

body: API version 2026 07 14 expands PortableImportRebinding.kind with four typed values: payment provider account email delivery route sms delivery route marketing integration Clients that exhaustively switch on rebinding kinds must handle these values before selecting the new API version. They replace ambiguous use of provider account for these resource classes. Existing provider account bundles remain readable for compatibility, but current Self Hosted exports use the typed values and require destination capability portable rebinding kinds v2 . Rebinding provenance now includes kind , and optional bindings may be supplied without becoming commit prerequisites. A material binding change still invalidates an existing approval and requires a fresh approval digest.

title: API migration from 2026-07-14 to 2026-07-15
description: Supply source-signed final cutover evidence for portable import commits.
body: API version 2026 07 15 adds the PortableCutoverProof schema and an optional request body to POST /migration jobs/{jobId}/commit . The body remains optional for non portable migration adapters. A tixkit portable job now requires: Generate the proof with createPortableCutoverProof from @tixkit/portability ; do not construct or sign an ad hoc JSON representation. The source observation must be no more than 60 seconds old when the destination validates it, the expiry window cannot exceed five minutes, and a full bundle must truthfully report sourceFrozen: true . Delta transports now carry the exact signed parentEnvelope ; imports without a matching parent fail preflight. The JavaScript SDK exposes client.migrations.commitPortable jobId, approvalConfirmation, cutoverProof . Continue using client.migrations.commit jobId for non portable migration adapters. Destinations must configure the source public key registry before accepting portable commits.

title: API migration from 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-16
description: Adopt principal-bound historical portability exports and signed organization identity.
body: API version 2026 07 16 adds historical export authorization and execution to the existing Self Hosted portability endpoint. Configuration exports remain the default and require no authorization: Historical exports are intentionally approval gated. An accepted organization owner or admin user first calls POST /portable export authorizations with the organization and an expiry no more than 24 hours in the future. The same user then supplies the returned single use authorizationId to POST /portable exports : Both export modes require Idempotency Key . Historical grants are tenant , organization , scope , and principal bound; they may be revoked before use and consumed by exactly one export job. A completed or crash recovered job replays its exact immutable signed bytes. A new artifact cannot be signed or published after authorization expiry. Portable manifest v2 now binds source.organizationId . Historical manifests additionally carry the exact grant identifier, tenant, organization, granting principal, grant time, expiry, and scope. Importers must continue validating the full manifest signature, payload checksums and safety attestations. Historical imports also require explicit historical import v1 destination entitlement; ticket bearer codes, plaintext provider references, credentials, payment tokens, and private signing keys are never transferred. The JavaScript SDK exposes client.portability.grantHistoricalExportAuthorization , revokeHistoricalExportAuthorization , and createExport . createExport returns the raw response so callers can stream or persist the signed bundle without JSON reserialization. This candidate remains unpublished and approval gated until the protected release and provenance checks are complete. Webhook test and delivery metadata Durable domain webhook payloads keep their independent 2026 01 01 envelope version. The synthetic test.ping.apiVersion field and the X Tixkit API Version header passed to delivery attempts now report 2026 07 16 ; these identify the HTTP/SDK test and replay contract, not a domain event schema migration. Consumers that assert those diagnostic values must accept 2026 07 16 . Signature verification, event subscription names, durable domain payload fields, retry behavior, and delivery ordering semantics are unchanged.

title: API migration from 2026-07-16 to 2026-07-17
description: Adopt durable exact-parent delta exports and final cutover receipts.
body: API version 2026 07 17 adds optional delta lineage to configuration portability exports. Existing full and historical export requests remain compatible. Create and retain a successful full export through POST /portable exports . For the next configuration export, call POST /portable delta exports and pass the durable job identifier as parentExportJobId : Tixkit reopens the immutable parent artifact, verifies its stored size and checksum, validates its Ed25519 signature and internal lineage, and requires the parent to belong to the same tenant, organization and source deployment. The new signed manifest binds the exact parent bundle, manifest SHA 256 and change cursor. Export sequence numbers are strictly increasing but may contain gaps after failed builds; identity comes from the signed parent tuple, not arithmetic adjacency. For the final delta after source writes are frozen, include the separately produced freeze receipt: cutoverFreeze is invalid without parentExportJobId . Historical exports cannot use delta lineage. Every request still requires Idempotency Key ; the parent and freeze receipt participate in the immutable request fingerprint, so substitution under the same key fails closed. The receipt hash is a signed manifest commitment, not destination authorization by itself. The destination separately validates its short lived signed PortableCutoverProof before commit. Activating that final delta makes the destination lineage terminal: later deltas and implicit full snapshot rebaselines fail closed. A new baseline requires a future explicit operator authorized rebase protocol. The runtime data schema advances to 0080 for durable destination lineage checkpoints. Destinations may import a signed 0079 parent followed by an 0080 delta, but newly produced exports require destination compatibility with 0080 . Keep the bundle signing key pinned for the complete cutover chain; the current exporter does not support changing that key between a parent and successor. The JavaScript SDK models full, delta and final delta requests as a discriminated union. Other SDKs retain their existing raw HTTP facilities until typed portability helpers are added. This candidate is unpublished and remains protected release approval gated. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . Synthetic test.ping.apiVersion and the X Tixkit API Version delivery attempt header now report 2026 07 17 .

title: API migration from 2026-07-17 to 2026-07-18
description: Adopt authenticated, bounded portable import artifact intake.
body: API version 2026 07 18 adds authenticated portable import upload contracts. Export, delta lineage and final cutover request shapes from 2026 07 17 remain compatible. The upload request is intentionally breaking for clients that used the previously open ended migration import purpose: destination organization scope is now mandatory and unrelated resource scopes are rejected. The candidate remains unpublished and requires protected release approval. Portable import uploads Portable bundle upload tickets now use purpose migration import . The request must include organizationId and sizeBytes ; brandId and eventId are rejected. The caller needs migrations.write , and the service resolves the tenant and organization before issuing a signed upload. The maximum portable artifact size is 50 MiB. Clients must send one of the documented portable bundle media types and preserve the exact byte length and checksum through upload completion. Import registration accepts only the completed, clean artifact selected by the signed manifest and consumes it once while creating the job file link and audit event atomically. Use the upload lifecycle in this order: 1. Request a migration import upload ticket for the destination organization. 2. Upload the exact artifact bytes to the returned signed URL. 3. Complete scanning and checksum verification. 4. Register the artifact with the portable import job. 5. Start preparation only after registration succeeds. Artifact retention is lease based. Active preparation and commit may renew a recently active artifact, but no new work starts after the absolute 90 day retention ceiling. A missing, substituted or inconsistently linked artifact fails closed and enters retention hold where applicable. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . Synthetic test.ping.apiVersion , SDK version headers and the X Tixkit API Version delivery attempt header report 2026 07 18 .

title: API migration from 2026-07-18 to 2026-07-19
description: Adopt sponsor-bound agent principal and delegation controls.
body: API version 2026 07 19 adds the experimental, private beta agent principal and delegation control surface. Existing 2026 07 18 operations remain compatible; this is an additive contract release. Agent identity and delegation The new bearer authenticated operations register and inspect explicitly sponsored agent principals, grant bounded event delegations, and revoke principals or delegations. They require a human principal with tenant wide developers.write . API keys, mobile principals, system principals and brand or event scoped users cannot administer agents. Registration accepts a caller owned stable reference, agent kind, capabilities and maximum autonomy. The service returns a tenant namespaced principal identifier and derives the tenant, sponsor, protocol version, active state and registration time. Managed Cloud accepts third party agents in this beta; a Self Hosted deployment may additionally enable self hosted agents. Delegations accept the returned principal identifier, one or more supported capabilities, explicit event: scopes and an expiry no more than 30 days in the future. The service rechecks the sponsor's current permissions and accepted organization membership inside the database transaction. It derives the issue time and permission snapshot; clients cannot supply either value. Every mutation requires an Idempotency Key containing 16–255 characters. Reusing a key with different intent returns a conflict. Principal revocation atomically revokes active delegations. Consequential execution remains approval gated and is outside these registration operations. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . Synthetic test.ping.apiVersion , SDK version headers and the X Tixkit API Version delivery attempt header report 2026 07 19 .

title: API migration from 2026-07-19 to 2026-07-20
description: Adopt organizer-controlled, separately retained agent memory.
body: API version 2026 07 20 adds the experimental, private beta organizer memory surface. Existing 2026 07 19 operations remain compatible; this is an additive contract release. Organizer memory Human sponsors can create, inspect, correct, export and delete workspace or event scoped memory through /v1/agent memory . The service derives the tenant, sponsor, identifier, organizer provenance time and content digest. Clients cannot submit those ownership or integrity fields. Every operation, including reads and exports, requires a 16–255 character Idempotency Key because access is audited. Corrections and deletions require the current expectedVersion . Deletion physically removes the retained content while immutable audit rows preserve digests rather than memory text. The recurring Temporal maintenance workflow erases expired entries in bounded, retryable and idempotent batches. Workspace memory requires settings.write or tenant wide developers.write . Event memory requires events.write or tenant wide developers.write , and resource scoped users can address only an event in their current scope. The repository rechecks live user state, permission grants, sponsor ownership and resource identity inside its transaction. The supported content kinds are organizer preferences and project context . Credential like values, personal contact data and other prohibited sensitive content fail closed. Retention is explicit and bounded by the shared protocol. The JavaScript SDK exposes these methods under tixkit.agentMemory : create , inspect , export , correct and remove . Use the authenticated human sponsor's accessToken ; do not pass an API key or the sponsor credential to an agent process. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . Synthetic test.ping.apiVersion , SDK version headers and the X Tixkit API Version delivery attempt header report 2026 07 20 .

title: API migration from 2026-07-20 to 2026-07-21
description: Adopt explicit third-party agent authentication and isolated agent sessions.
body: API version 2026 07 21 adds sponsor created OAuth credentials for explicit agent principals and the first agent authenticated route. Existing 2026 07 20 operations remain compatible; this is an additive experimental/private beta release. Create an agent credential A human sponsor with live tenant wide developers.write calls POST /v1/agent principals/{id}/oauth clients with an organization used only for credential administration, a display name and a 16–255 character Idempotency Key . The agent must be active, belong to the same tenant and be sponsored by the caller. The service rechecks the sponsor's active profile, permission grant and accepted organization membership inside the transaction. The response contains a clientId , fixed agent.invoke scope and a clientSecret shown exactly once with Cache Control: no store . An identical replay returns the same credential metadata without the secret. Create another client before revoking an old one to rotate credentials without a shared secret or source fork. Generic /v1/oauth applications management exposes only resource owner applications. Agent clients remain behind the sponsor bound, idempotent and immutable agent control lifecycle. Exchange client credentials Send grant type=client credentials to POST /v1/oauth/token . Authenticate with HTTP Basic client secret basic or JSON/form client id and client secret fields, never both. Credentials are not accepted in the query string. An active client for an active agent receives a tk aat ... bearer token with exactly ten minutes of database clock lifetime, fixed agent.invoke scope and no refresh token. Use the token with GET /v1/agent/session . The response identifies the agent principal and deliberately reports an empty product permission set. Authentication is separate from delegation: every typed action must still satisfy the intersection of agent capability, sponsor authority, a current delegation, tenant policy, action risk policy and resource state. All other authenticated routes deny agent principals unless the route explicitly opts into agent access. Revoking either the client or the principal takes effect on the next request because authentication joins the live token, application and principal records. The JavaScript SDK exposes sponsor operations through tixkit.agentControl.createOAuthClient and revokeOAuthClient . Server side agents use tixkit.agentAuth.exchangeClientCredentials , then construct a client with the returned access token and call tixkit.agentAuth.session . Agent client secrets are rejected in browser runtimes. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . Synthetic test.ping.apiVersion , SDK version headers and the X Tixkit API Version delivery attempt header report 2026 07 21 .

title: API migration from 2026-07-21 to 2026-07-22
description: Adopt immutable agent action preparation and server-authoritative event publish dry runs.
body: API version 2026 07 22 adds immutable typed action preparation for experimental agent integrations. Existing 2026 07 21 operations remain compatible; this is an additive private beta release. The agent protocol advances from 2026 07 11 to 2026 07 22 because event.publish now requires an exact readiness snapshot digest in its canonical payload. The prior schema remains immutable and available at the versioned package export. Migration 0082 agent actions advances existing server managed principal records to the new protocol version; agents should inspect GET /v1/agent/session and accept only the advertised literal before preparing actions. Prepare an event publish action Authenticate with an explicit tk aat ... agent access token, then call POST /v1/agent/actions with a 16–127 character Idempotency Key and exactly these fields: Do not send an agent or sponsor identifier, tenant, resource version, policy version, API operation, readiness payload or timestamp. The server derives those bindings from current database state inside a serializable transaction. Unknown or cross tenant resources return not found without exposing their existence. The response contains the canonical typed action, its SHA 256 digest, expiry, authorization evidence and an event readiness dry run. Persist the entire response. An exact idempotent replay returns the original action and evidence; changing intent under the same key returns an idempotency conflict. Retrieve the same immutable evidence with GET /v1/agent/actions/{actionId} using the same agent identity. The JavaScript SDK exposes these operations as tixkit.agentActions.prepare and tixkit.agentActions.get . Approval remains mandatory authorization.eligibleForApproval is not execution authority. It means the live intersection of agent capability, sponsor permission, delegation, tenant policy, action risk policy, resource version and readiness passed except for the mandatory human approval. A later approval must bind to the exact actionDigest ; any material change requires a newly prepared action and fresh approval. Public approval, revocation and execution lifecycle endpoints are not part of this release. Do not invoke an internal executor or publish an event based only on preparation evidence. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . Synthetic test.ping.apiVersion , SDK version headers and the X Tixkit API Version delivery attempt header report 2026 07 22 .

title: API migration from 2026-07-22 to 2026-07-23
description: Adopt short-lived human approval bound to an immutable agent action digest.
body: API version 2026 07 23 adds human approval for an immutable prepared agent action. Existing 2026 07 22 operations remain compatible; this is an additive private beta release. Agent protocol 2026 07 22 remains current because approval binds to the existing canonical action digest without changing its schema. Approve an exact prepared action Authenticate as the action's human sponsor. The user must have an accepted organization membership and current events.write permission for the action's event. Call POST /v1/agent/actions/{actionId}/approvals with: a unique 16–127 character Idempotency Key ; X Tixkit Confirmation: approve: : ; and a strict JSON body containing only the prepared action's exact actionDigest . The JavaScript SDK exposes the operation as tixkit.agentActions.approve and derives the confirmation header from those exact inputs. Inside one serializable transaction, Tixkit locks the tenant and action and revalidates the explicit agent principal, sponsor identity, delegation, tenant membership, event permission, resource version, policy version, action risk and readiness digest. The server derives the approver, permission snapshot, approval time and expiry. The approval expires after at most five minutes and is uniquely bound to one tenant action. An exact idempotent replay returns the original approval even after authority changes; it does not grant new authority or extend expiry. Reusing a key with different action, digest, actor or permission snapshot conflicts. A new request after any material authorization, policy, resource or readiness change fails closed. Execution remains unavailable Approval is immutable authorization evidence, not direct execution. Action bound revocation and the public execution lifecycle are not part of this release. Do not publish an event by writing to the database, calling an internal executor or bypassing the existing API/workflow boundary. Migration 0083 agent approval action unique enforces at most one action bound approval per tenant action across supported database drivers. Legacy approvals without an action binding remain readable for compatibility but cannot authorize this agent action flow. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . title: API migration from 2026-07-23 to 2026-07-24
description: Adopt action-bound revocation for unconsumed agent approvals.
body: API version 2026 07 24 adds revocation for an unconsumed agent action approval. Existing 2026 07 23 operations remain compatible. Revoke one exact approval Authenticate as the action's original human sponsor and call POST /v1/agent/actions/{actionId}/approvals/{approvalId}/revoke with: a unique 16–127 character Idempotency Key ; X Tixkit Confirmation: revoke: : : ; and a strict JSON body containing only the exact actionDigest . It never expands authority. Tixkit serializably locks the tenant, action and approval, then binds the tenant, sponsor, action, approval and digest. Cross sponsor, cross tenant, changed binding and consumed approval requests fail closed. Exact replays return the original revoked approval; competing keys cannot create a second lifecycle event. title: API migration from 2026-07-24 to 2026-07-25

body: API version 2026 07 25 adds durable execution for an approved immutable event.publish agent action. Existing 2026 07 24 operations remain compatible. The serialized agent protocol remains 2026 07 22 ; the new HTTP operation scopes durable execution idempotency to the explicit agent principal without requiring principals to negotiate a new protocol literal. No database or agent protocol migration is required for this additive operation. The JavaScript SDK exposes this operation as tixkit.agentActions.execute . Do not send sponsor identity, tenant, resource version, policy version, operation or readiness data. Those bindings remain server authoritative. The operation atomically consumes the exact unrevoked approval and creates durable execution evidence. Before the product effect, Tixkit rechecks the explicit principal, sponsor, delegation, tenant and risk policy, current permission and membership, resource and policy versions, approval binding and readiness digest. Changed authority fails closed. An exact terminal replay returns the same execution. A concurrent retry may receive 409 while another worker holds the execution lease; retry the identical request. One execution records at most one event publish effect. Failed responses expose a bounded failureCode , not provider or database detail. Execution idempotency is derived from the authenticated agent and original preparation key. Different agents may safely use the same preparation key without colliding. title: API migration from 2026-07-26 to 2026-07-27
description: Persist and inspect immutable, approval-aware agent plans through the shared Platform API.
body: API version 2026 07 27 adds immutable agent plan creation, scoped inspection and compare and swap state transitions. Existing 2026 07 26 operations remain compatible. Agent actions remain on protocol 2026 07 22 ; plan definitions and states use the additive shared plan protocol 2026 07 27 . Create an immutable plan Prepare every typed action first. Build a canonical plan definition whose step digests and identities match those actions, then call POST /v1/agent/plans or tixkit.agentPlans.create . Only the exact authenticated agent may create the plan. Tixkit reloads the bound actions and rechecks the agent, sponsor, delegation, capabilities, resource scopes, action digests and lifetime under a database lock. Creation stores an immutable definition, exact step to action bindings and a server timestamped initial state. It does not approve or execute an action. Exact idempotent replay returns the original initial state. A reused key with different intent returns conflict. Inspect and advance state The exact agent or human sponsor can call GET /v1/agent/plans/{planId} or tixkit.agentPlans.get planId . Cross tenant, cross agent and cross sponsor plans return not found. Responses use Cache Control: no store . Call POST /v1/agent/plans/{planId}/transitions or tixkit.agentPlans.transition with the expected state version, the complete next step state list, a bounded reason code and an idempotency key. Clients cannot submit evidence or timestamps. Tixkit locks and reloads the current plan, actions, approvals and executions, then validates dependencies, fresh approval binding, approval consumption, execution state and result digests before committing the next version. Every accepted transition records immutable before and after state plus canonical, digest bound actor authorization evidence. Material authorization changes fail closed. State version races return conflict and are safe to re read before retrying. Durable domain webhook payloads remain at envelope version 2026 01 01 . title: API migration from 2026-07-27 to 2026-07-28
description: Bind planned approvals, executions, audits and cancellation to the authoritative plan digest.
body: API version 2026 07 28 makes the existing plan digest safety contract executable end to end. The action protocol remains 2026 07 22 and immutable plan definitions remain readable at plan protocol 2026 07 27 . This release is compatible: it adds optional response/request properties at the HTTP schema level, while requiring the property only when an action is already bound to an authoritative plan. Approve a planned action Standalone actions continue to send actionDigest with confirmation approve: : . For an action bound to a plan, send both actionDigest and planSha256 . The confirmation must be approve: : : . Tixkit rejects an omitted or substituted plan digest, a plan or step outside awaiting approval , incomplete dependencies, an expired plan, or a changed action binding. Exact idempotent replay still returns the original approval without granting new authority. Persist and inspect execution evidence Migration 0085 agent execution plan binding adds nullable agent executions.plan sha256 . Existing standalone execution rows remain valid. New planned executions persist the exact approval and plan digest, and every lifecycle audit record must carry the same digest. Rollback refuses to discard populated plan bound evidence. The execution request remains { approvalId, actionDigest } ; do not send planSha256 there. The server derives it from the consumed approval. The JavaScript SDK accepts planSha256 only on agentActions.approve and constructs the exact planned confirmation. Cancellation and synchronous adapters The first public event.publish adapter returns a terminal result synchronously, so a plan may advance directly from awaiting approval to an evidence validated terminal state. This is compatible enforcement of the existing 2026 07 27 plan schema; serialized plan definitions and digests do not change. Cancellation and effect application serialize on the tenant boundary. Cancellation that commits first prevents reservation or product mutation. Once any bound execution exists, cancellation is rejected; clients must inspect the execution and record its exact terminal result instead of claiming that the effect was stopped. Durable domain webhook envelopes remain at 2026 01 01 . Synthetic test.ping.apiVersion , SDK version headers and X Tixkit API Version report 2026 07 28 .

title: API migration from 2026-07-28 to 2026-07-29

body: API version 2026 07 29 adds a direct, read only readiness.read action. The action protocol remains 2026 07 22 , and immutable plan definitions remain at plan protocol 2026 07 27 . title: API migration from 2026-07-29 to 2026-07-30

The action protocol remains 2026 07 22 , immutable plan definitions remain at 2026 07 27 , and the action registry contract advances independently to 2026 07 30 . The 2026 07 29 event.publish , readiness.read , approval, execution and plan response schemas remain unchanged. Authorization is the intersection of: an active explicit agent principal with events.read capability; an active delegation containing events.read and event: scope; the sponsor permission snapshot and the sponsor's current tenant events.read grant; active sponsor identity and accepted organization membership; an allowing event.read action/risk policy; and exact current resource and policy versions. It excludes credentials, buyer data, payment data, arbitrary metadata, SEO fields and provider state. The action payload binds eventSnapshotSha256 to the canonical projection, while resultSha256 binds the complete result and observation time. untrustedContentPaths is always exactly 'event.title', 'event.description' . title: API migration from 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-01
description: Adopt approval-bound, version-safe event updates through the shared agent protocol.
body: API version 2026 08 01 adds the direct only, consequential event.update adapter. The action wire protocol remains 2026 07 22 , immutable plan definitions remain 2026 07 27 , and the action registry contract advances to 2026 08 01 . Every 2026 07 31 schema remains available unchanged. Prepare the exact update Send POST /v1/agent/event updates with an event scoped delegationGrantId , event resourceId , non empty changes , and an idempotency key. The accepted changes match the non status generic event PATCH surface. Identity, sponsor, tenant, version, policy, operation, and preparation time remain server owned. Preparation resolves slug, venue, owned media, dates, and normalized values through the organizer event update rules without mutating product state. The returned preview binds the current resource version, sorted changed fields, complete before/after projections, changePreviewSha256 , observation time, and untrusted content paths. previewSha256 binds the persisted preview as returned. Retrieve it with GET /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId} . The action is eligible for approval only when the active explicit principal and delegation contain events.execute , the exact event scope is present, the delegation snapshot and live sponsor both grant events:write , membership is accepted, and current tenant action and risk policies allow event.update . Approve and execute The exact human sponsor approves through POST /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId}/approvals , supplying actionDigest , a unique idempotency key, and confirmation approve: : . Approval is fresh, short lived, immutable, and records the exact events:write permission snapshot. Revoke an unconsumed approval through POST /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId}/approvals/{approvalId}/revoke . event.update is direct only in this release and cannot be inserted into an immutable plan. The explicit agent executes through POST /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId}/executions . Both Idempotency Key and X Tixkit Confirmation must equal execute: : : . Execution reloads and locks the event, principal, delegation, sponsor authority, policy, approval, and execution fence in a serializable transaction. It re resolves the original normalized changes, recomputes the exact preview digest, rejects a no op or any material drift, applies one compare and swap update, and atomically commits agent attributed product audit plus durable effect evidence. Retrieve immutable evidence through GET /v1/agent/event updates/{actionId}/executions/{executionId} . Success returns only { resourceId, resourceVersion, status: "updated" } , where the version is exactly the approved target version plus one. Exact retries converge on the same terminal execution and never apply the update twice. A version, preview, authority, policy, or approval change fails closed and requires a newly prepared action and fresh approval. Recovery and reversal Recovery accepts only an effect whose execution fence, action identity, resource identity, result digest, live event version, and complete approved projection all match. It never trusts an execution shell or caller supplied tool result. Infrastructure failures before the atomic product transaction remain resumable; committed effects reconcile without reinvocation. Automatic compensation is not available. A reversal is another consequential event.update against the new version and requires its own exact preview and fresh approval. Pin the registry through @tixkit/agent protocol/schemas/agent action contracts/2026 08 01 and the full action overlay through @tixkit/agent protocol/schema or ./schemas/2026 08 01 . title: API migration from 2026-08-05 to 2026-08-06
description: Adopt logical event-media references and portable content documents.

headings.text: Store media roles, not delivery URLs

body: API version 2026 08 06 adds role based event media to event page content and advances portable configuration exports to data schema 0081 . The retained 2026 08 05 API contract remains available. Store media roles, not delivery URLs Event page image fields may store tixkit:event media:poster , tixkit:event media:cover , or tixkit:event media:social . The organizer editor resolves these references through authenticated preview renditions, while the public event surface resolves the exact role through public immutable renditions. Missing or removed roles clear only the affected image; the rest of the published page continues to render. Private organizer paths, upload artifact paths, object URLs, credential bearing URLs, and secret bearing query strings fail closed on public pages and social metadata. Publishing locks the event, document, and selected version in one transaction, validates every logical media reference against the event scope, and advances the public event revision atomically. Attaching or removing media uses the same event lock, so an approved document cannot race a media change into publication. Upgrade portable destinations to schema 0081 New configuration and historical exports declare: API version 2026 08 06 ; data schema 0081 as both the minimum and maximum; capabilities portable bundle v2 , portable rebinding kinds v2 , and portable content documents v1 . Destinations must advertise the exact data schema and all required capabilities before preflight. Schema 0081 includes scoped content documents and their immutable version bodies. Event page logical media references remain logical across export and import, while owned media bytes travel as separately signed and checksummed assets. Destination import validates content again before any canonical write, removes stale unreferenced versions on replay, and blocks rollback when assets, render artifacts, or test sends still reference an imported version. Publication state is intentionally inert. Exports omit publication pointers and publication timestamps, and imports restore every document and version as a draft. Review and publish imported content explicitly at the destination. Rendition variants are unchanged from 2026 08 05 . Imported event media now generates the same thumbnail , card , page , and social WebP set used by native uploads, with checksum addressed immutable object keys.

headings.text: Consume one evaluated snapshot at a time
