title: Performance budgets
description: Review documentation and platform performance contracts and the commands that reproduce them.
body: Performance claims require measured evidence. Repository budgets cover the configured application routes and documentation specific search/reference behavior. The docs architecture budgets compressed search bootstrap and shards, search open interaction, initial JavaScript, layout stability, content paint, and API reference loading. The OpenAPI JSON is downloadable but is not loaded on ordinary guide pages; the local search index loads only after search intent. Trusted database regression jobs retain three fresh process samples and a deterministic aggregate for PostgreSQL and MySQL. The aggregate binds the commit, runner label, pinned database image, workload, complete metric set, and checksums, and reports per metric min, median, p95, and max. Every individual sample must remain inside the absolute budget. These checksums provide integrity detection, not a producer signature or independent authenticity proof. Authenticity depends on the trusted workflow and retained artifact controls. This evidence detects regressions for the committed workload on the trusted runner. It does not prove deployment capacity, soak stability, fault behavior, or real user experience. Historical median comparison is supported only when an explicitly retained baseline from the same runner, database, workload, and metric set plus a committed regression threshold are supplied; the compared Git revisions are expected to differ. Immutable cross revision baseline publication is not yet a CI gate. The scheduled trusted workflow also runs committed PostgreSQL and MySQL regression scenarios. Each scenario requires four bounded bursts spaced across 30 minutes and binds the revision, trusted runner label, pinned database image, workload and explicit trusted single host regression profile. It fails closed on incomplete duration, missing or extra metrics, source metrics mismatch, identity drift, timeout, invalid or incompatible retained baseline, median regression and evidence directory reuse. All evidence produced before a failure plus a bounded failure record is uploaded; raw metrics, sealed samples and aggregates exist only when execution reaches those stages. This scheduled evidence improves regression ownership but is not soak or trend evidence and is not a supported profile capacity envelope. The single trusted host is not the Production Kubernetes profile, retained GitHub artifacts are not immutable baseline publication, and these runs do not establish production fault behavior, RUM or long term trend availability. The separate weekly/manual capacity workflow characterizes the controlled trusted runner label with serial PostgreSQL and MySQL profiles, four increasing concurrency points and three fresh process samples per point. It classifies only inventory exhaustion with zero availability as expected decline; another rejection is a platform failure. It records both total request and successful reservation throughput, and saturation uses only successful reservation throughput and latency so fast sold out responses cannot improve the result. Any sample p95 or platform failure breach, or the first median successful throughput gain below its threshold, establishes saturation. It emits a bounded claim only when saturation follows a lower publishable point; no observed saturation means no capacity claim. That artifact's literal scope is trusted single host capacity characterization . It explicitly denies Production, Cloud, Compact and general capacity. Git/config/workload/raw hashes are checksums, not signatures, and workflow retention is not public immutable evidence. It assumes the runner label remains mapped to the same controlled machine; hardware is not fingerprinted, so evidence is invalid after runner remapping or host drift. A failed workflow uploads a checksummed diagnostic marker with phase and step outcomes. It binds the config checksum only after checkout succeeds, is not schema validated capacity evidence and cannot carry a capacity claim. Browser measurements use the lockfile pinned Playwright Chromium installed on the trusted runner by the repository runtime installer. Record environment, commit, viewport, browser, sample count, and artifact when reporting a regression. Do not convert an unmeasured target into a success claim.

title: Self-hosting architecture
description: Map Tixkit applications, durable services, trust boundaries, and public ingress before deployment.
body: Tixkit runs separate API, Temporal worker, admin, checkout, and documentation processes. PostgreSQL is the primary documented local path; repository validation also covers declared compatible database modes. Redis supports runtime coordination, Temporal owns durable workflows, and S3 compatible storage owns generated/uploaded artifacts. Trust boundaries Expose only required public ingress: buyer checkout/public API, authenticated admin/API, provider webhooks, and documentation. Keep database, Redis, Temporal service, and object storage administration private. The API authenticates and scopes requests. The worker consumes trusted Temporal tasks but still calls scoped repositories/providers. Browser applications never receive database, provider, API key, or signing secrets. Failure boundaries API health does not prove worker readiness; worker health does not prove provider readiness. Monitor each service plus database, Redis, Temporal, storage, authentication, payments, messaging, and webhook delivery independently. Continue with configuration and secrets /self hosting/configuration .

body: Tixkit supports clerk , oidc , and the development only dev provider. Select a provider | AUTH PROVIDER | Intended use | Production behavior | | | | | | clerk | Clerk sessions for the organizer dashboard and API | Requires all Clerk keys and a verified identity sync webhook. | | oidc | Bearer JWTs from a standard OIDC issuer | Requires an HTTPS issuer, audience, and pre linked Tixkit profiles. | | dev | Deterministic local development principal | Refuses to start outside development and is forbidden in production. | Development defaults to dev when AUTH PROVIDER is unset. Other environments default to clerk . Set NEXT PUBLIC AUTH PROVIDER to the same value anywhere the admin browser bundle is deployed; never let the browser and API select different providers. Configure Clerk Provide server secrets only to the API and worker. The publishable key is safe for the admin browser bundle. Create a Clerk webhook endpoint at POST https://api.example.com/v1/webhooks/clerk and subscribe it to: user.created user.updated user.deleted organization.created organization.updated The route requires svix id , svix timestamp , and svix signature , verifies the raw request body with CLERK WEBHOOK SECRET , rejects timestamps outside the replay window, and deduplicates the Svix message ID before starting the identity sync workflow. A missing webhook secret returns 503 WEBHOOK NOT CONFIGURED ; unsigned identity updates are never accepted. Clerk organizations map to Tixkit organizations. Clerk users map to user profiles , while active organization memberships and permission grants remain authoritative. Missing or suspended profiles fail closed. If a user spans tenants, the active Clerk organization or an explicitly authorized tenant selection must disambiguate the request. Configure OIDC OIDC mode verifies API bearer JWTs against the issuer JWKS and the configured audience: The token must contain a stable sub . Tixkit looks up the external identity as oidc: : in user profiles.clerk user id ; create that mapping through an authorized provisioning process before cutover. email is useful for audit display but is never a safe identity join key. The optional org id or organization id claim must match an accepted Tixkit organization membership. When one subject has profiles in multiple tenants and no organization claim selects one, the caller must send X Tenant Id ; otherwise authentication fails as ambiguous. Suspended profiles, absent mappings, invalid issuer/audience, unaccepted memberships, and missing permission grants fail closed. The optional tenant id claim is only a hint and does not override database grants. OIDC mode supplies API authentication. Before using it for the organizer dashboard, verify that your deployment's browser sign in integration obtains and forwards the expected bearer token; the repository does not infer a browser session from an arbitrary issuer. Rotate credentials safely For Clerk server and publishable keys: 1. Create the replacement keys in Clerk. 2. Deploy the new CLERK SECRET KEY , CLERK PUBLISHABLE KEY , and NEXT PUBLIC CLERK PUBLISHABLE KEY together. 3. Verify a fresh login, session refresh, GET /v1/me , tenant selection, and a permission denial. 4. Revoke the old keys only after every API, worker, and admin instance uses the replacement. For the Clerk webhook secret, create or rotate the endpoint secret, deploy the new CLERK WEBHOOK SECRET , send a signed test delivery, and confirm identity sync before retiring the old endpoint. The verifier accepts one active secret, so use a second endpoint or a coordinated delivery pause when overlap is required; do not revoke the old secret before the new deployment is ready. For OIDC signing keys, rely on the issuer's JWKS overlap and cache window. Test tokens signed by the replacement key before the issuer removes the old key. Changing OIDC ISSUER URL changes the external subject key and therefore requires an explicit profile mapping migration. Cut over and roll back Stage mappings before changing provider selection. Never create cross tenant memberships from an email match. In a production like environment, prove login or bearer authentication, logout/session expiry where applicable, profile suspension, organization selection, multi tenant ambiguity rejection, permission denial, and audit attribution. Keep the prior provider configuration recoverable until those checks pass. To roll back, restore both AUTH PROVIDER and NEXT PUBLIC AUTH PROVIDER , restore the matching secrets, restart the API/admin/worker, and repeat the denial and tenant selection checks. Do not delete old identity mappings until the retention and rollback window closes.

title: Back up and restore Tixkit
description: Protect relational data and object artifacts with measured, rehearsed recovery procedures.
body: Backups are not complete until a restore rehearsal proves usable application state. Protect database data and required object storage artifacts; document which ephemeral Redis/Temporal state is reconstructed and which durable Temporal persistence is protected by its own service plan. Backup Run the repository's engine/object storage backup procedures with encrypted destinations, least privilege access, retention, and monitoring. Record timestamps and non secret artifact identifiers. Compact operators use bun run compact:backup and bun run compact:restore . The Compact runbook /self hosting/compact defines the artifact contents, checksum gate, and Temporal volume boundary. Restore rehearsal Restore into an isolated environment, run migrations only as required by the target commit, start API/worker/application processes, and verify tenant scope, a representative event/order, artifact download, workflow visibility, and health checks. Measure recovery point and recovery time from actual rehearsal evidence. Do not publish invented RPO/RTO claims. Production recovery contract Production backups must land in a failure domain independent from the primary services, use an identified encryption policy/key, and be signed with a manifest key stored separately from the artifacts. The scripts refuse to create a Production artifact unless DR BACKUP DESTINATION CLASS=independent , DR BACKUP ENCRYPTION , DR MANIFEST SIGNING KEY , DR MANIFEST KEY ID , and DR SOURCE RELEASE are explicit. Use bun run dr:backup:production with executable DR QUIESCE COMMAND and DR RESUME COMMAND controls. While writes and workers are quiesced, the command captures exactly one configured relational engine, owned object storage, and provider executed Temporal checkpoint metadata under one recovery point timestamp. DR TEMPORAL CHECKPOINT COMMAND must return a verified immutable ID, namespace, and exact recovery point. Redis is explicitly reconstructible state, not a recovery source. The command always attempts to resume writes on failure. Each artifact has a mandatory SHA 256 sidecar and a signed, versioned manifest binding its name, kind, size, checksum, recovery point, source release, encryption policy, and independent destination class. A checksum without a valid manifest signature is insufficient. The Production bundle additionally requires DR BACKUP PUBLISH COMMAND , DR BACKUP RECEIPT VERIFY COMMAND , and DR BACKUP RETRIEVE COMMAND : the publisher must return an immutable provider receipt with different plaintext/ciphertext hashes and a provider signature, the provider specific verifier must cryptographically validate that receipt, and retrieval must reproduce the signed plaintext exactly. Plaintext staging is then removed. Merely setting an “encrypted” environment label is not accepted as proof. Backup output directories must be caller owned and mode 0700 or stricter. Artifacts and sidecars are published exclusively at mode 0600 ; existing paths, symlinks, inode substitution, concurrent publication, and partial publisher/retriever failures fail closed. Provider hooks execute with an explicit environment allowlist and never receive the manifest signing key. Staged restore and cutover Never point a restore command at the active database or bucket. PostgreSQL and MySQL restores require DR ISOLATED TARGET=1 and reject a non empty target before mutation. PostgreSQL restores are transactional. Object restore requires a new RESTORE S3 BUCKET , rejects traversal, links, devices, duplicate paths, and oversized expansion before extraction, mirrors with deletion semantics, and requires an exact post copy diff. Production MySQL recovery additionally requires verified identity TLS, an authenticated short lived provisioning receipt, DR MYSQL TARGET LEASE COMMAND , DR MYSQL TARGET LEASE VERIFY COMMAND , and DR MYSQL FAILED RESTORE CLEANUP COMMAND . The lease holder must atomically consume the provisioning nonce and hold or renew an exclusive provider lease bound to the artifact SHA 256, opaque restore target ID, server UUID, database, and unique attempt ID. Tixkit verifies the lease before import, periodically during import, after import, and before evidence; loss or expiry terminates the import and requires independently checked cleanup. The lease is released only after signed evidence or verified cleanup. A boolean “isolated” assertion or an empty table query alone is not sufficient. Production object recovery requires workload identity, metadata restore, a run owned bucket creation receipt, independent ownership verification, remote inventory reconciliation, and failed bucket cleanup plus independent absence verification. Destructive cleanup is armed only after the ownership verifier binds the exact endpoint, bucket, and restore run nonce. An existing bucket or a failure before ownership proof is never cleanup authorized. Metadata hooks never receive the reconciliation output path; the inventory verifier returns its result on stdout and the parent exclusively writes mode 0600 evidence binding the verifier hash and signed inventory. Every restore requires an executable DR VERIFY COMMAND . This verifier must check tenant/event/order/ticket/payment invariants, owned object references and checksums, Temporal visibility/replay expectations, API and worker health, and representative checkout, webhook, check in, and export behavior. When DR EVIDENCE FILE and DR INCIDENT AT are supplied, the restore signs evidence binding the artifact, target, source/target releases, verifier hash, recovery point, execution duration, measured RPO, and incident to recovery RTO. Future incident timestamps are rejected. Use bun run dr:restore:production after the independent retrieval/decryption step. Supply opaque, non secret DR DATABASE TARGET ID , DR OBJECT TARGET ID , and DR PRODUCTION TARGET ID values; database URLs and credentials are deliberately excluded from evidence. Before any component mutation, a provider authenticated target receipt must bind the physical application database, object store and Temporal persistence identities. DR PRODUCTION TARGET LEASE COMMAND must atomically acquire one renewable provider claim for that target triplet, while its independent verifier proves the live holder and fencing generation throughout restoration. Restore hooks receive the authenticated Temporal checkpoint through an anonymous read only capability instead of the mutable extraction path; Linux seals the capability against writes, growth, shrinkage, and further seal changes. Hooks must consume that capability once per phase and keep any private parsed representation within the hook process. DR TEMPORAL EVIDENCE VERIFY COMMAND independently authenticates provider restore evidence and binds its immutable ID, namespace, workflow/run identity and recovery point to the backup checkpoint. The command safely extracts the outer bundle, rejects missing or extra artifacts, verifies every nested signature and shared recovery point/source release, restores all three isolated targets, and runs final live cross store reconciliation. It writes signed component evidence plus an aggregate production.json whose hashes bind the publication receipt, exact retained object version, target claim, consequential adapters and all component results. Provider claim completion is a separate durable transition after production.json . It must atomically validate the live holder and fencing generation, bind the exact aggregate evidence hash, and return the same authenticated receipt on an identical retry. DR PRODUCTION TARGET CLAIM QUARANTINE COMMAND quarantines an unfinished claim during controlled failure. If the provider committed completion but the local process stopped before writing or verifying its receipt, run bun run dr:finalize production restore claim with the original evidence directory and provider completion/verifier commands; it verifies the signed aggregate and bound lease before recovering the receipt. Never retry restoration over an ambiguous active claim. After review of the signed aggregate production.json and authenticated completed claim receipt, use bun run dr:promote restored target . Promotion refuses component only or unfinalized evidence. Operator supplied commands atomically rebind the destination and verify the promoted runtime. If cutover or verification fails, the command restores and verifies the previous binding. Signed promotion evidence pins the completed claim receipt and verifier, target, bundle, aggregate hash and fencing generation alongside every cutover/rollback command. The staged target and previous target remain available until the retention policy permits deletion. Migration rollback rehearsal bun run dr:migration rehearsal requires three distinct URLs: source, empty forward clone, and empty rollback clone. Supply separate opaque FORWARD TARGET ID and ROLLBACK TARGET ID values for evidence. It backs up the source, restores and verifies the forward clone, executes the real forward migration without loading .env.local , verifies the new version, then restores and verifies a second old version clone. DR EXPECT FORWARD FAILURE=1 exercises failure injection and still executes restore based rollback. PostgreSQL and MySQL must each pass this rehearsal. These commands make local and production like drills reproducible. The repository safety suite proves fail closed contracts with controlled adapters, including concurrent MySQL lease contention, object cleanup authorization, lease/checkpoint loss, and crashes before provider completion, after provider completion, and before local completion verification. The opt in bun run test:production dr:integration gate exercises digest pinned MySQL 8.4/MinIO and Temporal 1.24/PostgreSQL 16 component recovery plus one real outer production backup.sh → immutable independent publication → source destruction → production restore.sh round trip. The outer proof migrates and seeds real Tixkit tenant/event/media state, restores distinct application and Temporal PostgreSQL systems plus MinIO, permits exactly one concurrent mutating winner, reconciles live application/media/workflow state, recovers the exact retained provider version after a newer overwrite, denies replay and wrong key retrieval, and proves idempotent durable claim finalization. This is real local provider proof, not production like Kubernetes, managed provider, zone/dependency, upgrade/rollback, or EPYC RPO/RTO proof; C 019 and C 119 remain open for those external gates.

title: Run the Compact profile
description: Start, operate, back up, restore, upgrade, and remove a complete single-host Tixkit installation.

headings.text: Isolated installations on one operator host

body: Compact is the supported single host profile for evaluation and smaller installations. It runs the API, worker, admin dashboard, checkout, migrations, seeded evaluation data, PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, Temporal UI, and S3 compatible object storage. It is not highly available and does not run MySQL alongside its default PostgreSQL database. Host envelope Use a 64 bit Linux host or Docker Desktop with at least 4 CPU cores, 8 GiB of memory, and 30 GiB of free disk. Building all application images is resource intensive; 8 cores, 16 GiB of memory, and 60 GiB of free disk is the recommended starting envelope. Measure your own event, checkout, workflow, media, and retention load before production use. Move to the Production profile when you need multiple hosts, independent scaling, managed backing services, availability guarantees, or formal disaster recovery objectives. First start From the repository root: compact:init writes infra/compact/.env with mode 0600 , a deployment identity, project scoped source build image names, and unique persistent service and Ed25519 portability signing keys. Only the API receives the bundle, payload and dry run private keys plus cutover public trust needed by its current runtime routes; migration, seed, storage init and worker containers do not receive those private keys. The generated cutover private key remains host local for future source side exchange tooling and is not injected into a container. Back up this file separately; it contains private keys and must not be committed or shared. External source key registration and destination worker import trust are not configured by this bootstrap step. In the default source mode, compact:up builds the application images. It then applies idempotent migrations, creates the object bucket, seeds an evaluation organization and event, and waits for every service health condition. The source build names are deliberately separate from the public release contract. To consume a published version instead of building the checkout, initialize with image mode release version : Release mode validates the four stable tixkit/ : references and pulls them without a local build. A protected release or operator may replace each generated TIXKIT IMAGE value with its corresponding tixkit/ @sha256: reference from the release manifest. The current frontend images compile their API origin at build time, so release mode deliberately fails closed unless the default project and port layout is retained; it cannot be co hosted with a second Compact release installation yet. Source mode is required for custom ports and isolated installations on one host. This constraint prevents a pulled admin or checkout image from silently routing to the wrong API. Environments created before image modes existed continue to use the historical default project and local build tags without rewriting their secrets. The default endpoints are: checkout: http://localhost:3000 admin: http://localhost:3001 API readiness: http://localhost:4000/ready Temporal UI: http://localhost:8080 MinIO console: http://localhost:9001 In source mode, edit the non secret PORT values in infra/compact/.env before compact:up when a host port is already occupied. Frontend API URLs are baked into their images, so rerun compact:up after changing API PORT . Release mode rejects any port change until published frontends support runtime API origin configuration. Isolated installations on one operator host Every Compact lifecycle command accepts env file and project name . The environment file records its Compose project name, so containers, networks and named volumes do not overlap. Use distinct host ports for installations that run at the same time: Edit the destination PORT values before starting both projects. When changing MINIO API PORT , set S3 PUBLIC ENDPOINT to the exact matching http://localhost: origin; validation rejects mismatches so browser signed uploads cannot reach another local installation. Always pass the matching environment and project flags to compact:up , compact:status , compact:logs , compact:backup , compact:restore , compact:upgrade and compact:uninstall . Compact rejects a project name override that does not match the owner recorded in the selected environment. Each project also receives distinct local application image tags, preventing one installation's frontend build and baked API URL from replacing another installation's restart image. Operate compact:restart removes and recreates the profile containers without rebuilding images or deleting the four named data volumes. This reruns migrations, storage initialization and the idempotent seed before waiting for every long running service to become healthy. Restarting the host or Docker also preserves the named volumes; use compact:restart afterward for the supported full profile restart check. From a fresh authoritative public clone on a host that meets the minimum envelope, retain a machine readable lifecycle proof with: The output directory must be new, outside the repository and beneath a real non symlink parent. The proof command refuses a dirty, shallow, non public or already initialized clone, and requires HEAD to equal the object currently advertised by the named authoritative public branch or version tag. It records the remote ref/object, exact commit/tree, host and Docker envelope, all 13 service states, seed persistence, restart, backup/restore, live database/object fingerprints for every negative restore case, Temporal dependency failure/recovery, upgrade, validation commands and a mode 0600 transcript. Raw daemon metadata is omitted and the transcript fails closed if it contains generated credentials. A passing local artifact is still not hosted publication, high availability, legal or Production profile proof. Trust a portability source On the source Compact host, write the public identity artifact: For an isolated non default installation, pass its environment explicitly: The command prints the artifact's SHA 256. The JSON contains only the deployment identity and Ed25519 public keys, plus a self signature proving possession of the advertised bundle key. Send the JSON and its printed SHA 256 to the destination over separate authenticated channels. The self signature detects modification but does not establish trust by itself; the destination operator must verify the expected SHA 256 out of band. On the destination Compact host, install trust for that exact source. Set the capacity to the number of bytes actually available to Tixkit owned object storage, excluding the space needed for databases, logs, backups, and upgrades: The trust command verifies the checksum, strict artifact schema, bundle key self signature, distinct Ed25519 role keys, current API/data schema pair, and different source/destination deployment identities and authorities. It then atomically adds only source public keys and destination compatibility policy to the mode 0600 environment. The worker receives the resulting import trust; the API receives the source cutover public key. Source private keys never enter the artifact or destination. A destination has one explicitly selected import source at a time. Replacing it requires replace , followed by compact:up ; retain the verified artifact and checksum with the migration change record. Concurrent trust changes fail closed. No existing infra/compact/.env.portability.lock is removed automatically. If the trust process is forcibly terminated, verify from the recorded PID that no trust process is running before removing the lock manually. Back up and restore The backup quiesces the application and workflow tier, then captures the application database, both Temporal databases, and owned object storage as one logical snapshot. Its manifest records the Tixkit version, source commit, byte counts, and SHA 256 checksums. Restore verifies the exact artifact set, checksums, version, and archive entry safety, restores into temporary databases and a temporary bucket, and validates their required schemas before cutover. It retains rollback databases and objects until the complete profile is healthy. Keep backup directories and infra/compact/.env encrypted outside the host's failure domain. Compact Redis state is reconstructible and is not backed up. Upgrade and uninstall After checking out the reviewed target release: The command creates a checksummed pre upgrade backup, pulls current base images, rebuilds the application images from the checked out release, reapplies migrations, and waits for health. Test restore before upgrading important installations. Remove containers while preserving data and secrets with bun run compact:uninstall . Destructive removal is explicit: The destructive form removes Compact volumes and its generated environment file. Verify an external backup first.

title: Configure services and secrets
description: Validate environment contracts for API, worker, applications, databases, providers, signing, and storage.
body: Start from .env.local.example for local development and your platform's secret manager for deployed environments. Never commit a populated environment file. Validate by mode Use the mode matching the environment. Production checks are intentionally stricter and must not be bypassed with local capture values. Separate public and private values Only variables explicitly designed for public browser use may use a public prefix. Database URLs, provider secrets, webhook secrets, API keys, encryption/signing material, object storage credentials, and Temporal credentials remain server only. Rotate a secret after suspected exposure and restart/redeploy every process that consumes it. Verify old credentials no longer authenticate. Set DASHBOARD CURSOR SIGNING KEY to at least 32 random characters in every deployed API replica. All replicas in one environment must share the same value so organizer action cursors remain verifiable across requests. Rotating it intentionally invalidates every outstanding dashboard cursor; clients then refresh the first page. Configuration drift Record non secret environment contracts in deployment configuration, validate them before release, and compare API/worker settings that must agree, including database, Temporal namespace/task queue, storage, and provider mode. After every required mode passes, continue to the deployment runbook /self hosting/deployment .

title: Choose and operate a database
description: Use only the database modes covered by Tixkit migrations, repositories, and compatibility validation.
body: PostgreSQL is the default local path. MySQL and MSSQL behavior is limited to the compatibility explicitly exercised by repository migrations and tests. Do not infer support for an untested engine/version from Kysely's general capabilities. Provision safely Use TLS, private networking, a least privilege application identity, bounded connection pools, monitored storage, and automated backups. Keep migration credentials separate when the application identity should not alter schema. Validate compatibility Run the engine specific migration and integration gates documented by the repository before adopting a version or managed service. Test timestamps, JSON, indexes, locking, pagination, unique constraints, and rollback/forward behavior with production like settings. Operational rule Never repair application state by editing production rows without an approved runbook, backup, tenant scope, and verification plan. Prefer supported API, repository, workflow, and compensation paths.

title: Microsoft SQL Server status
description: Understand the implemented SQL Server dialect surface and its gated validation status.
body: PostgreSQL is Tixkit's reference database and MySQL is the tier one parity target. Microsoft SQL Server support is experimental: the dialect and correctness helpers exist, but operators must not infer full production parity from the presence of the driver. Configure the driver Set DB DRIVER=mssql and provide DATABASE URL MSSQL : The URL parser also accepts mssql:// . The Kysely dialect uses tedious with tarn pooling. DB DRIVER=sqlserver is accepted as an alias. Implemented surface packages/db/src/dialects/mssql.ts provides: | Helper | Purpose | | | | | parseMssqlConnectionUrl | Parse SQL Server URLs into tedious connection settings. | | createMssqlDialect | Create the Kysely dialect and pool. | | createMssqlLimitPlugin | Rewrite select limits to TOP or OFFSET FETCH . | | mssqlObjectIdExists | Generate OBJECT ID existence checks. | | mssqlDropTableIfExists | Generate conditional table drops. | | buildMssqlMergeUpsert | Generate MERGE upserts. | | mssqlForUpdateTable | Add WITH UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK to locking reads. | | executeMssqlForUpdate | Execute a locked read through Kysely. | SQL Server migrations must use explicit existence checks and foreign key cleanup order. Upserts use MERGE ; correctness critical locking reads use WITH UPDLOCK, HOLDLOCK instead of SELECT ... FOR UPDATE . Validate an installation Run the local static and unit gates first: Then run the gated integration suite against a disposable SQL Server instance: CI runs the SQL Server job only when RUN MSSQL TESTS is enabled. A production decision requires current migration, rollback, concurrency, API, workflow, backup, and restore evidence for the exact SQL Server version and topology; the dialect unit suite alone is insufficient.

title: Deploy Tixkit
description: Build, migrate, release, smoke-test, and roll back the API, worker, applications, and documentation coherently.
body: Deploy immutable artifacts built from one reviewed commit. The API, worker, OpenAPI reference, SDK compatibility statements, dashboard, checkout, and docs must describe the same contract. Use the Compact profile /self hosting/compact for a complete supported single host evaluation or smaller installation. Use the Production profile and externally operated backing services for high availability and independent scaling. Follow the dedicated Production profile runbook /self hosting/production for compatibility, sizing, secret, migration, network, observability, and recovery gates. The Production chart is infra/helm/tixkit with values production.yaml . It intentionally refuses placeholder image digests, bundled datastores, unrestricted network CIDRs, automatic migration hooks, missing observability, and incomplete ExternalSecret mappings. Supply release manifest image digests and environment specific ingress, database, and service egress ranges; do not weaken these checks with a copied evaluation file. For External Secrets, reconcile the ExternalSecret and wait for its target Secret before running infra/scripts/run helm migration.sh . The runner validates the chart derived key inventory, acquires an atomic migration lock, applies the release scoped database egress policy, creates a uniquely named bounded Job, waits for completion, and prints current logs. It fails rather than reusing a completed Job or overlapping another migration. This local runner evidence does not replace a production like install, upgrade, rollback, and recovery rehearsal. Release order 1. Back up and verify restore readiness. 2. Run the release dry run and documentation/OSS export gates. 3. Apply forward compatible migrations using the approved migration identity. 4. Deploy API and worker with compatible Temporal workflow code. 5. Deploy admin, checkout, and docs. 6. Verify health, representative public/authenticated reads, checkout, workflow, webhook, and documentation routes. Rollback Roll back application artifacts independently only while contract and migration compatibility permits it. Prefer a forward fix for destructive schema changes. Preserve documentation redirects so dashboard links remain valid across a docs rollback. Smoke checks Verify /health for API and docs, worker readiness, a real published test event, authenticated context, and a test safe checkout. A green homepage is not a complete deployment proof. Continue with observability configuration /self hosting/observability before accepting the release.

title: Configure object storage
description: Store uploads and generated artifacts in a private S3-compatible bucket with controlled download paths.
body: Configure endpoint, bucket, region, access key, and secret only on server processes that require storage. Use a least privilege identity restricted to the intended bucket/prefix. Keep the bucket private. Public or authenticated download behavior must flow through the API's documented allowlisted or signed routes; object keys are not authorization. Validate upload, durable read, signed download expiry, public allowlist behavior, deletion/retention, and failure recovery. Monitor capacity, error rate, and credential expiry. Include required artifacts in backup/restore rehearsals rather than assuming database backups are sufficient.

title: Configure observability
description: Monitor request, workflow, datastore, provider, export, checkout, and documentation health without logging sensitive data.
body: Collect service level metrics, traces, structured logs, and health signals for the API, worker, admin, checkout, docs, database, Redis, Temporal, storage, and configured providers. Correlate safely Use request, workflow, delivery, export job, checkout session, and order identifiers only where policy permits. Redact authorization headers, cookies, API keys, signing secrets, provider credentials, ticket codes, and personal data payloads. Alert on outcomes Alert on error/latency saturation, worker/task queue lag, failed checkout finalization, payment reconciliation, webhook dead letters, export failures, database pool pressure, storage errors, and documentation smoke failures. Avoid alerts based only on process uptime. Link alerts to the exact incident runbook /operations/incidents and verify alert routing during release rehearsal. Production Helm contract The Production values require observability to remain enabled. Configure OTEL EXPORTER OTLP ENDPOINT in the runtime Secret with an HTTPS collector origin; Tixkit appends /v1/traces . If the collector requires headers, set OTEL EXPORTER OTLP HEADERS as comma separated, URL encoded key=value entries. Header values are credentials: keep them in the Secret, never in OTEL RESOURCE ATTRIBUTES or committed values. The chart fixes the supported transport to http/protobuf , uses parent based ratio sampling, and labels telemetry with the tixkit service namespace and deployment profile. Change the sampling ratio only after checking collector capacity and trace cost. When observability.metrics.mode=service monitor , the cluster must already have the Prometheus Operator CRDs. The chart creates: an API ServiceMonitor for /metrics using METRICS BEARER TOKEN from the runtime Secret; alert rules for sustained API 5xx rate, API p95 latency, and stalled durable migration progress; worker metric delivery through PROMETHEUS PUSHGATEWAY URL . Workers publish under a per pod Pushgateway grouping, delete that grouping on graceful shutdown, and bound migration stall alerts by the grouping's push time seconds . This prevents a hard lost pod's last gauge from alerting forever; monitor Pushgateway storage separately and retain its own stale series cleanup policy. If another metrics system owns discovery, set the mode to external and reproduce the same authenticated scrape and alert semantics outside the chart. Never expose /metrics through public ingress. Before accepting a release, prove a trace reaches the collector, an authenticated scrape succeeds while an unauthenticated scrape returns 401 , worker activity metrics arrive, and a test alert reaches the intended route. A rendered ServiceMonitor alone is not runtime proof.

title: Run the Production profile
description: Configure, size, upgrade, and recover the high-availability Kubernetes profile.
body: The Production profile is the high availability Self Hosted path. It requires Kubernetes 1.30 or newer so the scheduler enforces the chart's stable two domain minDomains topology contract. It consumes immutable public images and requires external PostgreSQL or MySQL, Redis, Temporal, object storage, secrets, telemetry, and backup services. It does not install evaluation datastores. Compatibility contract Pin one public Tixkit release manifest and keep its API image, worker image, migration image, admin image, checkout image, OpenAPI version, migration range, and Temporal workflow code together. The chart requires digest addressed images. Validate PostgreSQL 16 or MySQL 8.4, Redis 7, a compatible Temporal 1.24+ service or Temporal Cloud namespace, and the target S3 compatible API in a staging cluster before production adoption. A provider claiming protocol compatibility is not proof; run the repository's database, Temporal replay, object, and provider failure suites. Do not roll application images behind an incompatible schema or workflow deployment. Use the upgrade runbook /self hosting/upgrades , and retain the prior public release manifest and restored target until post cutover verification completes. Initial sizing tiers These are load test starting points, not capacity guarantees: | Tier | API | Worker | Admin | Checkout | Starting use | | | | | | | | | Small | 2 × 250m CPU / 512 MiB | 2 × 250m / 512 MiB | 2 × 200m / 384 MiB | 2 × 200m / 384 MiB | Staging and smaller steady workloads | | Medium | 3–6 × 500m / 1 GiB | 3–8 × 500m / 1 GiB | 2–4 × 250m / 512 MiB | 3–8 × 300m / 512 MiB | Multiple concurrent onsales | | Large | Result of measured load/soak tests | Separate task queues and measured concurrency | Measured dashboard traffic | Measured burst concurrency | High volume or event day peaks | Keep at least two replicas, topology spreading, disruption budgets, bounded autoscaling, and enough cluster headroom to replace one failure domain. Size relational connections, Redis, Temporal task queues, object throughput, OTLP, and Pushgateway alongside pods. Run checkout/inventory concurrency, webhook replay, check in sync, exports, and failure injection at the intended peak plus safety margin; record saturation and recovery, then set requests, limits, HPA bounds, and worker concurrency from that evidence. Installation controls Start from infra/helm/tixkit/values production.yaml . The chart fails when image digests, operator selected network CIDRs, manual migration strategy, observability, or required external secret mappings are absent. For External Secrets, reconcile the secret, run infra/scripts/run helm migration.sh , and only then install or upgrade workloads. The migration runner uses a lock, unique Job, isolated egress policy, and current logs; it never reuses an old completed Job. Production renders zero unavailable rolling updates with a replacement surge, a readiness dwell, a bounded progress deadline, at least two replicas per workload, a disruption budget below the minimum replica count, and a hard topology spread minimum of two zones. A digest change rolls the relevant workload; a chart managed ConfigMap change changes the pod template checksum and rolls all four workloads. After an external Secret value changes, explicitly restart and verify the affected workloads because the chart cannot hash provider owned secret contents. Run the production conformance harness first without disruption, then with its exact destructive acknowledgement. Use a dedicated production like cluster and an operator owned evidence directory: The harness refuses a context mismatch or existing evidence file, verifies digest pinned images, replica/readiness, HPA bounds, rollout bounds, disruption headroom, the live two zone topology constraint, and Ready pod placement across distinct node zones. It binds cluster, namespace and Helm release identity, submits one policy eviction per workload only after the explicit acknowledgement, waits for a distinct Ready pod UID and fully observed deployment replacement, and writes before/after JSON without secret values. This is pod replacement evidence only; it does not replace zone loss, dependency, upgrade, rollback or cross store DR drills. Use the signed Production cluster rehearsal contract https://github.com/tixkit/tixkit/blob/main/infra/production/README.md for the remaining cluster drills. It supports exact zone loss , dependency loss , and release upgrade rollback modes, requires a drill specific destructive acknowledgement, pins operator adapter bytes, binds prior and target public release manifests, records functional probe outage and recovery measurements, verifies rollback against live image and topology state, and publishes exclusive Ed25519 signed/checksummed evidence. Run dependency loss separately for the configured database, Redis, Temporal, and object storage. A valid local controlled adapter result is implementation proof only; C 119 remains open until the contract runs on a reviewed production like cluster and the independently expected proof verifies. Before accepting the release, prove pod replacement, zone disruption, dependency loss, retry recovery, upgrade, application rollback, staged data restore, failed cutover rollback, authenticated metrics, trace delivery, and alert routing. Record actual RPO/RTO from the backup and restore runbook /self hosting/backups and restore . Until those drills pass in the operator's environment, the profile is configured but not production proven.

title: Upgrade Tixkit
description: Rehearse contract, migration, workflow, SDK, documentation, and rollback compatibility before production rollout.
body: Read release and documentation changes for API, SDK, CLI, configuration, providers, migrations, and workflows. Build the sanitized OSS tree and run the release dry run before upgrading. Compact operators check out the reviewed target release and run bun run compact:upgrade . The command creates a pre upgrade backup before rebuilding, migrating, and waiting for the complete profile to become healthy. Rehearse Clone production like data into an isolated environment using the approved sanitization process. Apply migrations, deploy API/worker together where workflow compatibility requires it, then run checkout, order, webhook, export, check in, and docs smoke paths. Roll forward or back Confirm the old application can run against the new schema before treating binary rollback as safe. Preserve Temporal replay compatibility. When rollback is unsafe, use the documented forward repair and restore decision instead of forcing an older binary. Monitor errors, workflow failures, provider outcomes, and database performance through the rollout window.

title: Sell tickets with Tixkit
description: Create, publish, and operate an event with Tixkit's organizer tools.

headings.text: Start with a complete test event

body: Tixkit gives organizers one workflow for event setup, ticket inventory, checkout, orders, attendees, messaging, reporting, and event day operations. Availability: the managed Tixkit Cloud organizer experience is planned for an experimental private beta. It is not generally available, and this documentation does not promise hosted access, support terms, or a launch date. Start with a complete test event 1. Follow the Cloud organizer quickstart /sell/quickstart if you have a private beta invitation, or read it to understand the intended hosted journey. 2. Create your first event /getting started/first event , including ticket types and availability. 3. Complete a test checkout /getting started/test checkout before publishing or accepting live payments. 4. Review orders and fulfillment /operators/orders , attendee records /operators/attendees , and refund behavior /operators/orders/refunds . 5. Prepare check in /operators/check in , box office /operators/box office , team permissions, and incident ownership before event day. Operate the event Use the organizer dashboard for event configuration, schedules, ticket products, checkout forms, orders, attendees, messaging, and reports. Each operational guide identifies current stability and any provider dependent proof that remains. Managed organizer agents are also planned for an experimental private beta. title: Start selling with Tixkit Cloud
description: Follow the organizer-first hosted journey from an invited workspace to a test order.
body: Experimental private beta: Tixkit Cloud organizer access is not generally available. An invitation provides the sign in address, workspace, region, test payment policy, and support channel. Do not infer availability or create credentials from examples in public documentation. Accept the invited workspace Open the exact invitation link and confirm the expected workspace and organization before accepting. Use your own named identity; do not share an account. If the workspace, region, or role is unexpected, stop and contact the invitation's support channel. Create a test event Open Events , choose Create event , and use test safe content. Add a future occurrence, one ticket type with available inventory, a sales window that includes the current time, and the required checkout fields. Preview the buyer page before publishing. Follow Create and publish the first event /getting started/first event for the complete readiness checks. The dashboard must show the event as ready; do not repeatedly publish around an unresolved schedule, inventory, permission, or checkout form error. Complete a test order Use the payment mode assigned to the invited test environment. Never enter a live card or personal buyer data unless the invitation explicitly identifies an authorized production environment. Complete the test checkout journey /getting started/test checkout , then confirm the order, attendee, inventory change, and receipt state in the organizer dashboard. Prepare event day Review team permissions, refund policy, check in devices, connectivity fallback, incident ownership, and a representative test scan. Managed organizer agents remain a separate planned private beta and are not required for this journey. Continue Review orders /operators/orders , attendees /operators/attendees , check in /operators/check in , and reports /operators/reports and exports .

title: Support and responsible reporting
description: Choose the correct private or public channel for usage questions, defects, security issues, and documentation changes.
body: Use repository discussions or the documented support destination for usage questions that contain no private data. Use issue templates for reproducible public defects and documentation problems. Report security vulnerabilities privately through the process in SECURITY.md ; never open a public issue containing exploit detail, credentials, tenant data, or customer information. For an operational incident, follow incident runbooks /operations/incidents and your organization's escalation policy. Public community support is not a production paging service. When reporting a docs problem, include the canonical page URL, source path, version/commit when known, and the incorrect or missing outcome. Remove secrets, personal data, private topology, and internal payloads.
